## stdlib.kt { #stdlib-kt }

Matrix construction, terse numeric conversions and half-float packing.

[`mat4`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt--mat4) builds a transform from a base matrix, a translation, a rotation and a scale, all four
optional, so `mat4()` is the identity; [`mat3`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt--mat3) is its linear part, for normals and 2D transforms,
and ignores the translation it will accept. [`HasMatrix4f`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt-hasmatrix4f) is what anything able to hand out a
4x4 pose implements. [`fa`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt--fa) and [`ia`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt--ia) are array literals for `FloatArray` and
`IntArray`, and `Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d` are the conversions that keep Kotlin's numeric
widening out of the way in graphics code. `Vec2h`, `Vec3h` and `Vec4h` name the packed fp16
vector types, and `ByteBuffer.putf16` appends one half float, little-endian.

One of the `stdlib` files, which the `intro` preamble star-imports into every box, so everything
here can be called unqualified, with `Box` as the implicit receiver.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/math/linalg/stdlib.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/math/linalg/stdlib/)

## LanguageRuntimeSupport.kt { #languageruntimesupport-kt }

Shared machinery for a language runtime that converts a language root's children to its own
execution.

[`TopologyWatcher`](workspace.md#languageruntimesupport-kt-topologywatcher) runs a callback on the runloop whenever a session's box graph changes.
[`applyRuntimeToggle`](workspace.md#languageruntimesupport-kt--applyruntimetoggle) does the conversion: each child of a language root gets the runtime's
execution, a language label in its corner and the matching `code_language`. A child converts back
to Kotlin only when it has no language-root parent left, so the order of connecting and
disconnecting does not matter.

## MainLanguageRegistry.kt { #mainlanguageregistry-kt }

The registry that lets a box choose the language its children run in, such as Python instead of
Kotlin.

A language runtime registers itself with [`registerMainLanguageRuntime`](workspace.md#mainlanguageregistry-kt--registermainlanguageruntime). Every registered runtime
then gets a "Set Main Language: ..." command in the palette, next to "Set Main Language: Kotlin".
Running one on a selected box records the choice in the box's persistent `mainLanguage` property
and converts the box's children to that runtime. Choosing Kotlin clears the property and converts
them back.

[`AaCompletionClient`](workspace.md#aacompletionclient-kt-aacompletionclient) is consulted only when the AA completion backend is active, and returns null on
any failure so the caller falls back to the in-process K1 completer.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">AaCompletionClient</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/AaCompletionClient/#L63)

Stage C client for the out-of-process K2 Analysis-API completion endpoint (`/complete` on the code-use semantic sidecar). Used only when `KotlinEngineConfig.activeCompletionBackend == AA`; [`KotlinInterface2.complete`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt--kotlininterface2--complete) falls back to the K1 delegate whenever this returns null (no sidecar URL configured, HTTP/timeout failure, or the sidecar reports failure). The AA classpath stays out of the live runtime: this is a thin HTTP bridge, mirroring `CodeUseTelemetryService`.

## CommonMemberPrior.kt { #commonmemberprior-kt }

A ranking prior for the completion popup taken from a type's [`CommonMembers`](workspace.md#util-completion-kt-commonmembers) annotation, so that
an empty-prefix popup such as a bare `f.` lists the members that matter first.

[`CommonMemberPrior.rankOf`](workspace.md#commonmemberprior-kt--commonmemberprior--rankof) gives a member's declared position and [`CommonMemberPrior.scoreOf`](workspace.md#commonmemberprior-kt--commonmemberprior--scoreof) turns
it into popup points, below a user's own recency and above the category weight.

## CompletionAaE2EProbe.kt { #completionaae2eprobe-kt }

Runs Field's completion chain end to end against the Analysis-API sidecar, inside a live Field
JVM: a box's gathered preamble and this JVM's classpath go out over HTTP and the candidates come
back.

The probe switches the active backend to `AA`, builds a parent and a child box so the child
completes with an inherited preamble, and asks for candidates at a series of carets. Every check
names the backend that answered, read from `KotlinInterface2.lastCompletionBackend`, so an answer
the K1 fallback produced counts as a failure however good its candidates look. The fallback
offers every name in position, thousands of them, which is enough to satisfy a check for a
present candidate while the sidecar is still building its session.

A sidecar is required, and the smoke runner supplies one. By hand, point the probe at one with
`-Dafield.completion.sidecarUrl`, `AFIELD_CODE_USE_SEMANTIC_SIDECAR_URL`, or a
`build/completion-corpus/sidecar-url.txt`; with no sidecar it exits 3 and never prints its
`AA E2E DONE` marker, so the smoke gate reads an unreachable chain as a failure rather than as a
skip. A cold sidecar indexes the whole classpath before it can answer anything, which takes
minutes on the first request of its life and almost nothing once a running Field or an earlier
probe has paid for it, so waiting for the session is itself one of the checks. A run whose
candidate list came back truncated fails too: a receiver index too small for the classpath in
front of it drops real members, and nothing in the answer says which.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/completion/CompletionAaE2EProbe.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/CompletionAaE2EProbe/)

Sets `activeCompletionBackend = AA`, builds a parent→child box pair with an inherited preamble (as `CompletionContextProbe` does), and calls `KotlinInterface2.complete()` — which POSTs the box's gathered preamble + implicit `Box` receiver + this JVM's classpath to the sidecar `/complete`.

## CompletionCorpus.kt { #completioncorpus-kt }

A reproducible corpus of real boxes for measuring Kotlin completion, harvested with their macros
already expanded so each box sees the preamble it has at run time.

[`CompletionCorpus`](workspace.md#completioncorpus-kt-completioncorpus) reads the bundled starting points and templates, expands each box's macros without
evaluating its code, and checks the result in as fixtures that the completion probes measure against.

## CompletionCorpusHarvest.kt { #completioncorpusharvest-kt }

Builds the checked-in completion fixtures under `tools/completion-corpus/boxes`, and on a plain
run guards them instead of rewriting them.

The fixtures are real boxes, taken from the agent transcripts and templates in
[`CompletionCorpus.defaultDirs`](workspace.md#completioncorpus-kt--completioncorpus--defaultdirs), each with the preamble its parents give it. That preamble is what
makes a completion measurement about Field rather than about Kotlin, and recovering it means
reading whole documents and expanding their macros, so the probes downstream read it from disk
instead: [`CompletionLoweringProbe`](workspace.md#completionloweringprobe-kt-completionloweringprobe) measures against these files rather than harvesting its own.

This file's two jobs share one entrypoint, because a generator and the guard that watches for
drift have to agree on what the fixtures should contain. `AFIELD_HARVEST_WRITE=1` writes;
anything else compares, prints a `DRIFT` line per difference and fails. `AFIELD_LOWERING_CORPUS`
and `AFIELD_HARVEST_DIR` move the input and output directories.

A harvest resolves imports against the repository rather than against this machine, so a class
in `src/personal` that shares a simple name with one in `src/` cannot change what a fixture says
a box can see. Running with `AFIELD_IMPORT_HERMETIC=0` where that collision exists is refused
rather than recorded; `dev_docs/HERMETIC_COMPLETION_INPUTS.md` has the history.

## CompletionCorpusProbe.kt { #completioncorpusprobe-kt }

What Kotlin completion offers at a caret, read against what it ought to offer there.

Each fixture is a fragment of box code with `|` where the caret sits, and a list of candidates
the engine is expected to produce (goals) or to keep out (anti-goals). The matchers look for a
candidate by call form, by class, by exact text, by exact text ignoring case, or in the
named-argument form an editor offers for a parameter still to be filled in; they read the
candidate set and not its order, because the order a reader sees is decided in the browser by
`fieldSuggest.js` and is covered separately by `FieldSuggestPresentationTest`.

A run prints each goal as met or unmet, with the rank of the candidate that met it, and ends
with a met/unmet summary. It always exits 0, so the unmet set is a reading rather than a gate.
Completion is asked for through [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) itself, so the answers come from the engine a
box talks to and not from a stand-in.

The fixtures here are written out in this file. The box-shaped fixtures that
[`CompletionCorpusHarvest`](workspace.md#completioncorpusharvest-kt-completioncorpusharvest) generates, with a real inherited preamble, are what
[`CompletionLoweringProbe`](workspace.md#completionloweringprobe-kt-completionloweringprobe) reads instead.

## CompletionDocScrapeProbe.kt { #completiondocscrapeprobe-kt }

Asks how completion does on Field's own documentation: the fixtures are real doc code with the
caret put back where the author was typing.

`tools/scrape_completion_corpus.py` walks the Kotlin fences in `public/docs`, cuts each sampled
line at a member access, and records the member the page actually used into
`tools/completion-corpus/scraped.tsv` as a label, the code with a `‸` for the caret, and that
member's name. This probe replays each one through [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) and reports whether the
member came back and at what rank, with the top candidates printed under it so an answer can be
read rather than just scored.

Alongside the rank it reports whether the receiver type resolved at all, judged by how many
candidates came back: more than two hundred is read as completion having fallen back to offering
every name in scope. The two readings belong together, because a member can sit at a good rank in
a list that was never about the receiver.

It is a reading and not a gate: it always exits 0. With the scraped file absent it says so and
still prints its done marker, so the smoke entry shows that the probe ran rather than that it had
anything to run on.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/completion/CompletionDocScrapeProbe.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/CompletionDocScrapeProbe/)

## CompletionInteractionLogger.kt { #completioninteractionlogger-kt }

Durable, append-only observations of what happens at Field's autocomplete UI boundary.

The server cannot reconstruct this later: the browser merges several candidate sources and owns
the final ranking. Conversely the browser does not have the inherited preamble or the other
code-bearing properties that shape completion. [`record`](workspace.md#completioninteractionlogger-kt--completioninteractionlogger--record) joins those two views without placing
logging on the latency-sensitive completion reply path.

## GlslCompletionSupport.kt { #glslcompletionsupport-kt }

Completion and hover context for GLSL shader properties (`fragment`, `vertex`, `compute` and the
rest), including Field's `{% ... %}` and `{{ ... }}` shader template syntax.

[`GlslCompletionSupport.complete`](workspace.md#glslcompletionsupport-kt--glslcompletionsupport--complete) builds an inventory of the symbols visible in the shader (built-ins,
declarations and struct members from the box's own source and its shader template) and offers root
names, `receiver.member` completions, or template tags and expressions depending on the caret.
[`GlslCompletionSupport.describeContext`](workspace.md#glslcompletionsupport-kt--glslcompletionsupport--describecontext) answers the matching symbol-context request.

## KotlinSourceIndex.kt { #kotlinsourceindex-kt }

An on-disk index of the Kotlin definitions (top-level, nested and extension) under Field's source
roots, with each one's KDoc and completion category, which completion looks up by symbol name.

[`KotlinSourceIndex.startBackgroundSync`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt--kotlinsourceindex--startbackgroundsync) scans `src/jvmMain/kotlin`, `src/personal/kotlin` and
`src/generatedLinalg/kotlin` on a low-priority daemon thread and writes `kotlin_source_index.json`
under [`afield.ai.knowledge.FilestoreDir`](machine-learning.md#filestoredir-kt-filestoredir). Lookups go through [`KotlinSourceIndex.getKDocForSymbol`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt--kotlinsourceindex--getkdocforsymbol) and
[`KotlinSourceIndex.getCompletionCategoryForSymbol`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt--kotlinsourceindex--getcompletioncategoryforsymbol); [`KotlinSourceIndex.scanDefinitions`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt--kotlinsourceindex--scandefinitions) is the scan
alone, with no cache or network.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/completion/KotlinSourceIndex.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/completion/KotlinSourceIndex/)

started: [`BoxBodyRun`](workspace.md#boxbodyrun-kt-boxbodyrun) counts each box's nested body runs, and a source-backed block reads it to
refuse re-entering its own box.

## ReturnValueRegistry.kt { #returnvalueregistry-kt }

What happens to the value a box's code returns: [`ReturnValueRegistry`](workspace.md#returnvalueregistry-kt-returnvalueregistry) offers it to each
registered [`ReturnValueHandler`](workspace.md#returnvalueregistry-kt-returnvaluehandler) in turn, and the first one that accepts it keeps it running.

The handlers registered here run a returned `Sequence` one element per frame
([`registerSequenceReturnValue`](workspace.md#returnvalueregistry-kt--registersequencereturnvalue)) and a returned `frames { }` block ([`registerFramesReturnValue`](workspace.md#returnvalueregistry-kt--registerframesreturnvalue)).
Several values can be returned together with [`launches`](workspace.md#returnvalueregistry-kt--launches) or `+`, which builds a [`LaunchBundle`](workspace.md#returnvalueregistry-kt-launchbundle).
Each launch carries a per-strand generation, so relaunching or stopping a strand ends what it
started before.

## execution.kt { #execution-kt }

How a Kotlin box runs: [`KotlinExecution`](workspace.md#execution-kt-kotlinexecution) compiles and evaluates a box's code, launches what it
returns, and routes its printed output, errors and completions back to the editor.

[`BoxExecution`](workspace.md#execution-kt-boxexecution) is the contract a language engine implements: run a fragment or the whole box,
launch it on a strand, continue, stop, and answer completion and hover requests.
[`KotlinExecution`](workspace.md#execution-kt-kotlinexecution) is the Kotlin implementation. [`configureOutputProxies`](workspace.md#execution-kt--configureoutputproxies) connects a box's
`print`, error and `display(...)` output to the client that ran it. [`improveMessage`](workspace.md#execution-kt--improvemessage) and
[`suggestionsFor`](workspace.md#execution-kt--suggestionsfor) turn compiler diagnostics into the inline hints shown under an error.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/execution/execution.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/execution/execution/)

## playlist.kt { #playlist-kt }

Playlist functionality for Field4

This module provides helpers for executing boxes in a defined order based on their `playlist` property.
Boxes with a `playlist` property (a Double) will be executed in order from lowest to highest value.
Between each `begin()` call, [`executePlaylist`](workspace.md#playlist-kt--executeplaylist) waits `pauseList` `frame()` calls (default 1).

User-facing dev doc: dev_docs/Playlist.md (a pointer stub); this KDoc is the source of truth.

## stdlib_execution.kt { #stdlib-execution-kt }

Starting and stopping box code from inside box code, and the two block markers the editor reads.

`begin` runs another box's whole `code` property as if its run key had been pressed, on a named
strand, so a second launch on the same strand replaces the first; `end` stops every strand that
box is running and disposes any Field 4 renderer it owns. [`start`](workspace.md#stdlib-execution-kt--start) and [`animate`](workspace.md#stdlib-execution-kt--animate) open a [`Frames`](workspace.md#phased-kt-frames)
scope, the second re-entering its body every frame. `aside` holds a block an ordinary run skips
and option-return executes, which is where one-off experiments and debug dumps can live instead
of in a comment; `cell` marks a block as one notebook-style cell and at runtime only calls it.

One of the `stdlib` files, which the `intro` preamble star-imports into every box, so everything
here can be called unqualified, with `Box` as the implicit receiver.

## DataFramePluginCostProbe.kt { #dataframeplugincostprobe-kt }

Measures what wiring the Kotlin DataFrame compiler plugin adds to the cost of building a box's
Kotlin engine.

Field builds one [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) per box, so a compiler plugin registered into the compilation
state is paid for by every box in a document rather than by the boxes that use DataFrame. This
entrypoint builds three engines in a row, times each one's construction and its first evaluation,
and prints the per-engine total:

```diffstatic {data-lang=bash}
run-jvm-main afield.runtime.kotlin.DataFramePluginCostProbe --arg off
```

`--arg on` is the default and `--arg off` disables the plugin, by setting the
`afield.dataframePlugin` property that `KotlinInterface2.compilerPluginArgs` reads through a
`lazy`. The property has to be set before the first engine is built, which is why this is a
jvm-main entrypoint rather than something a box can call. The other half of the cost, the
`dataframe-core` jar every engine takes into its classpath snapshot, is fixed at build time, so
the difference between an `on` run and an `off` run isolates the plugin's share.
`dev_docs/DATAFRAME_PLUGIN.md` records the readings, and the different fix each of the two costs
would need if one ever came to dominate.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/kotlin/DataFramePluginCostProbe.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/DataFramePluginCostProbe/)

## DataFramePluginSpike.kt { #dataframepluginspike-kt }

Spike that measures what the Kotlin DataFrame compiler plugin can do inside Field's K2 REPL.

The plugin hangs off the compiler's function-call refinement extension, which the compiler
documents as "highly unstable and not recommended to use". At a call to a `@Refine`-annotated
function it interprets the arguments statically, computes the resulting schema, and rewrites the
call into a `run` block that casts it to `DataFrame<Token>` over **local** classes, because the
extension runs at body resolution and cannot create top-level declarations. The column accessors
are not declarations anywhere: they are a per-call-site local type plus an implicit extension
receiver injected by the plugin.

The probes ask how far that survives the REPL:

- within one snippet: a `dataFrameOf(...)` and a column access in the same evaluation, which
  shows whether refinement fires at all;
- a refined operation: `add("c") { a + b }`, a schema that changes, with the new column named
  only in the returned type;
- across snippets: the same two statements split across two evaluations of one engine, the
  boundary a box rerun has (boxes have separate engines, see [`SharedTypes`](workspace.md#sharedtypes-kt-sharedtypes)). The receiver
  injection only looks inside callable and code-fragment containers and a REPL snippet is
  neither, so the injected receiver is expected not to survive; the schema state rides on the FIR
  declaration itself, which is the mechanism that could carry it anyway;
- a shared `@DataSchema` interface, and one declared in a snippet.

Upstream's REPL work targets the Jupyter kernel, where cross-cell persistence comes from runtime
codegen of real top-level `@DataSchema` interfaces and the plugin's top-level generator is
switched off to avoid duplicating them (KT-77437). A within-snippet-only result here matches that
design.

The two invariants, that the plugin is passed to the compiler and its runtime is on the
classpath, fail the spike; the probes report either way.

## ExportedTypeNames.kt { #exportedtypenames-kt }

Renders the source-level type name that `@exported` writes into a consuming box's preamble.

`@exported` shares a value between boxes by two channels: the value itself crosses at runtime,
while its type crosses as text, a generated `val Box._x by InheritanceFromContext<T>()` line
spliced into the other box's preamble and recompiled by that box's own engine. This object
computes the `T`.

Each box has its own [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) with its own REPL history and snippet classloader chain,
so a type is usable in the consuming box only if two things hold:

- **It resolves at compile time.** Every engine's compile classpath is derived from the shared
  base classloader, so a type is nameable when that loader can reach it. Library types, `afield.`
  types and `@DependsOn` jars qualify; a class declared in another box's snippet does not, since
  it exists only in that box's snippet loader.
- **It is the same class at run time.** Snippet loaders are children of the shared loader, so a
  name that resolves there resolves to one `Class` for every box. The check is on class identity,
  so a shadowed name cannot produce a declaration that compiles and then throws
  `ClassCastException` where it is used.

A type that fails either test renders as [`ExportedTypeNames.OPAQUE`](workspace.md#exportedtypenames-kt--exportedtypenames--opaque) (`Any?`). A preamble line that
does not compile breaks every later compile in the consuming box, so a lost type costs less than
a wrong one.

Type arguments are walked recursively and each unnameable argument is erased on its own to `*`.
`List<Double>` stays `List<Double>`, and a list of a box-local class becomes
`kotlin.collections.List<*>`. [`ExportedTypeNamesSmokeTest`](workspace.md#exportedtypenamessmoketest-kt-exportedtypenamessmoketest) covers these cases.

User types declared in one box cannot pass these tests; sharing them needs a compilation unit on
the base classloader, which [`SharedTypes`](workspace.md#sharedtypes-kt-sharedtypes) is about.

## ExportedTypeNamesSmokeTest.kt { #exportedtypenamessmoketest-kt }

Smoke for [`ExportedTypeNames`](workspace.md#exportedtypenames-kt-exportedtypenames), which decides the type text `@exported` splices into another box's
preamble.

Two properties pull in opposite directions, and both are asserted here:

 - **Precision.** Library and `afield.` types survive with their generic arguments intact, so
   `List<Double>` reaches the consuming box as `List<Double>` rather than as `Any?`.
 - **Safety.** A type the consuming box cannot name degrades to `Any?` rather than being emitted
   and hoped for. A preamble line that fails to compile breaks every later compile in that box,
   so a false accept costs more than a false reject.

`testUnnameableArgumentIsErasedNotEmitted` is where the two meet: an argument the consuming box
cannot name collapses to a star projection, leaving `List<*>`, so the outer type still lands and
no unresolvable name reaches the preamble.

Pure renderer assertions: no REPL and no engine, so this stays fast. Runnable-object test style,
matching [`WitherSmokeTest`](workspace.md#withersmoketest-kt-withersmoketest).

## FieldKtParser.kt { #fieldktparser-kt }

Kotlin source to a parse tree, without compiling it.

Several things in Field need to look at the shape of box code rather than run it: reformat it,
find which imports it names, rewrite a call, translate it to JavaScript. Compiling is the
expensive way to get that, and it fails on code that does not yet make sense, which is most code
while it is being typed. This file holds the one parser they share: a `KotlinCoreEnvironment`
built once and reused, and a `parse` that returns the tree or throws on the first syntax error.

It is derived from ktfmt's own parser, and the Apache 2.0 notice above is ktfmt's.

## Kotlin24SyntaxSmokeTest.kt { #kotlin24syntaxsmoketest-kt }

Smoke test that a box compiles Kotlin 2.4 syntax: collection literals, positional
destructuring with square brackets, and name-based destructuring with renamed entries.

One snippet on a fresh [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) declares a data class, a `[1, 2, 3]` list literal and
both destructuring forms, and the test checks the result string. It runs in the smoke catalog
as `core.kotlin-2-4-syntax.smoke`.

## KotlinInterface2.kt { #kotlininterface2-kt }

The K2 implementation of [`KotlinScriptEngine`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt-kotlinscriptengine): the engine that compiles and runs a box's Kotlin.

Each box gets its own [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2), with its own REPL history and snippet classloader. It
compiles snippets with the K2 compiler, evaluates them, tracks the variables and functions they
declare, and answers completion requests in the editor. Redeclaring a plain `var` resets older
mutable bindings of the same name and Kotlin type after evaluation; captured `val`s stay fixed.

## KotlinLineNotes.kt { #kotlinlinenotes-kt }

Line notes for a Kotlin box: each top-level `val` or `var` a run declared, and the value it held
when the run finished.

The REPL hands back only a snippet's final value, but it also publishes the snippet's properties
after every evaluation (`box.ki.context.vars`, the same map `fromContext()` searches), so a
declaration's value can be read back by name once the run is over. A statement that declares
nothing has no note: its value was never kept.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/kotlin/KotlinLineNotes.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinLineNotes/)

## KotlinScriptEngine.kt { #kotlinscriptengine-kt }

The common interface every box's Kotlin engine implements, and the shared pieces both engines use.

[`KotlinScriptEngine`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt-kotlinscriptengine) is what a box's code runs through: compiling, evaluating, completion and
context tracking. [`createKotlinScriptEngine`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--createkotlinscriptengine) returns the active implementation, [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2)
(K2) or the older [`KotlinInterface`](workspace.md#kotlininterface-kt-kotlininterface) (K1). The file also holds the types both engines return, such as
[`CompletionResult`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt-completionresult), [`KotlinContext`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt-kotlincontext) and [`KotlinDebugScriptTracker`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt-kotlindebugscripttracker), and the compiler options they
share.

| <a id="kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--armbootstrapgate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">armBootstrapGate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L144) | Arm the engine's bootstrap-readiness gate (make it pending) so ordinary [`exec`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--exec)/`evaluate` block until [`bootstrap`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--bootstrap) (or [`releaseBootstrapGate`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--releasebootstrapgate)) opens it. Call this right after building an engine that will be bootstrapped asynchronously. Engines left un-armed (the default) never block — used directly in tests and ad-hoc snippet execution. No-op for engines without such a gate. |
| <a id="kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--releasebootstrapgate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">releaseBootstrapGate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L151) | Open the engine's bootstrap-readiness gate unconditionally, in case [`bootstrap`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--bootstrap) never ran (e.g. the box was tombstoned before it could) — otherwise a later [`exec`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--exec)/`evaluate` would wait forever. Idempotent; a no-op for engines without such a gate. |
| <a id="kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--complete"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">complete</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cursor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CompletionResult</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L153) |  |
| <a id="kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--warmcompletion"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletion</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L162) | Eagerly build whatever machinery [`complete`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--complete) needs (for K2 this is the K1 completion delegate — a full intro+preamble compile). Doing it up front, on the same main-runloop dispatcher [`complete`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--complete) uses, gets the one heavy compile out of the way outside any re-entrant runloop pump, so later completions are light and single-threaded-safe. Idempotent; a no-op for engines with no lazy completion bootstrap. |
| <a id="kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--warmcompletionbackend"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletionBackend</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">timeoutMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">120</span><span class="n">&#95;000</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L175) | Build the *serving* completion backend, not just the fallback. |
| <a id="kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--warmcompletionasync"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">warmCompletionAsync</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/KotlinScriptEngine/#L184) | Fire-and-forget proactive warm: schedule [`warmCompletion`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--warmcompletion) on the main-runloop dispatcher so the one heavy K1 bootstrap happens *before* the first completion/error-suggestion request rather than blocking it. Idempotent and self-de-duplicating (a no-op while a warm is already in flight, and cheap when already warm for the current preamble). Called on interactive code edits so the intelligent-error path is warm by run time. No-op for engines with no bootstrap. |

list survives a restart, and the server's Maven requests call into it.

## ReplBootstrapGateTest.kt { #replbootstrapgatetest-kt }

Smoke test of the bootstrap ordering of a [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) engine: the stdlib intro is
evaluated before any ordinary snippet.

On one engine the K2 evaluator chains each snippet's classloader onto the previously evaluated
snippet and emits the shared `ReplState` holder only into the first-evaluated one, so snippets
have to evaluate in the order they compile. A box launched under a running renderer evaluates
the intro asynchronously while its launch setup evaluates the inherited preamble, and the two
can race.

The race depends on timing, so the test does not rely on threads to reproduce it. It runs three
cases:

1. It forces an out-of-order evaluation and checks that it evaluates with the right answer, which
   it does since the Kotlin 2.4.20 uplift.
2. It checks that the engine's bootstrap gate ([`KotlinScriptEngine.armBootstrapGate`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--armbootstrapgate) and
   [`KotlinScriptEngine.bootstrap`](workspace.md#kotlinscriptengine-kt--kotlinscriptengine--bootstrap)) holds an ordinary exec until the gate is released.
3. It checks that a concurrent exec waits for the bootstrap to finish.

Like [`CompiledSnippetTest`](workspace.md#compiledsnippettest-kt-compiledsnippettest) it is a runnable object rather than a JUnit class.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/kotlin/ReplBootstrapGateTest.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/ReplBootstrapGateTest/)

## ReplRerunCompileCacheSmokeTest.kt { #replreruncompilecachesmoketest-kt }

Smoke test of the rerun compile cache: a rerun of an unchanged snippet is evaluated again
without compiling, its body really runs, and every change that would make a recompile bind
differently compiles.

The launch path runs the regathered preamble and then the box code through
[`KotlinInterface2.exec`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt--kotlininterface2--exec) on every rerun; this test drives the same calls on one engine. It covers an
edited body, a changed preamble, a changed expansion, the snippet evaluated last, a different
property, a new engine, a disposed engine, and the cache switched off with
`KotlinEngineConfig.rerunCompileCache`.

## ReplSnippetDeclarationsSmokeTest.kt { #replsnippetdeclarationssmoketest-kt }

Smoke test of what a box may declare at its top level and still compile under the K2 REPL.

Each case is a shape of ordinary box code that the stock 2.4 K2 REPL fails to compile or load,
and that Field's Kotlin fork (and, for the last group, Field's build of the Wither plugin) handles:

1. **A named function that touches the implicit `Box` receiver**, such as
   `fun foo(a: Double) = a + _qqq`. The fork stores the receivers in the snippet class's
   implicit-receiver fields, as the `.kts` script lowering does. Cases A, B, and case L, which
   checks that a later run binds `foo(12.0)` to the live declaration.
2. **An expression-bodied function that reaches the receiver**, such as
   `fun f(a: Double) = println(a)`. Only an inferred return type takes this resolution path, so
   the same body in braces is a separate shape. Cases S, T, U.
3. **A delegated property whose provider declares `provideDelegate`**, such as
   `var x by keyCamera()`. Cases N, Q.
4. **A destructuring declaration with a `_` entry**, such as `val (a, _) = p`. The fork builds the
   `_` entry as a local of the snippet's evaluation body rather than a class property. Cases V to
   Y, with Z1 to Z4 covering the name-based forms that reach the same path.
5. **A statement-level call to a function with no `callableId`**: a local function, or a member
   of a local or anonymous class, which Wither's IR pass has to tolerate. Cases LF1 to LF9.

One case is still open: a declaration from an earlier snippet can shadow a later one of the
same name, and the test records that behaviour rather than asserting a fix.

Each case drives the real engine: a fresh [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) with an implicit `Box` receiver, the
stdlib `intro`, then [`standardExecutionPractice`](workspace.md#macros-kt--standardexecutionpractice), the same preamble-then-body snippet sequence a
launched box runs through.

## RerunCompileCache.kt { #reruncompilecache-kt }

Compile once, re-evaluate on rerun: one K2 engine's record of the snippets it has compiled.

A box that reruns with exactly the same expanded source (a `propDown` reader re-launched by its
writer, the regathered preamble in front of it) can evaluate the snippet it already has instead
of compiling it again.

On Kotlin 2.5.0-Beta1's `K2ReplEvaluator`, re-evaluating an old `LinkedSnippet` is *not* the same
as recompiling its source, in two ways, and the cache refuses both:

 1. **The body does not run** when the snippet is re-evaluated straight after its own previous
    evaluation: the evaluator reuses the class it already loaded, and a K2 snippet's body runs
    once per loaded class. (`lst.add(1); lst.size` gave 1 twice and the list kept one element.)
    With any other snippet evaluated in between the class is reloaded and the body runs. So a
    hit is refused when the cached snippet is the evaluator's last one ([`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2) checks).
 2. **Stale bindings.** A snippet binds each name it uses to the snippet *class* that declared it
    when it was compiled. If a later snippet redeclares that name, a recompile binds the new
    declaration and a re-evaluation keeps the old one (`q * 2` stayed 10 after `val q = 6`). So
    every entry records which earlier snippet classes it references, and is refused once any
    name those classes declare has been redeclared by a later compile.

Mutable declarations and their readers also compile afresh: cached evaluation can reload
historical backing classes, leaving captured mutable slots outside the evaluator's current
history.

Also refused, conservatively: sources that carry `@file:` annotations (`DependsOn` refines the
compile configuration) — and a compiled `import` invalidates every entry, since imports may
change how already-compiled names would resolve now.

Everything here runs under the engine's compile mutex.

## SharedTypes.kt { #sharedtypes-kt }

Lets several boxes in one document use the same Kotlin class, with its real type.

Call [`sharedTypes`](workspace.md#sharedtypes-kt--sharedtypes) on a box with Kotlin declarations as source. [`SharedTypes`](workspace.md#sharedtypes-kt-sharedtypes) compiles them as
ordinary classes onto a classloader every box shares, so a `data class` declared there can be used,
and named, in any box. By default, publishing restarts the other boxes that have already run, because
a loaded class cannot be replaced.

## SharedTypesClasspathSpike.kt { #sharedtypesclasspathspike-kt }

Spike that measures whether a shared declarations directory can carry user-defined types
between boxes.

Each box has its own [`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2), so a type declared in one box's snippet is invisible to
every other box (see [`ExportedTypeNames`](workspace.md#exportedtypenames-kt-exportedtypenames)). The proposed fix compiles such types as ordinary Kotlin
into a directory hung off the process-wide shared classloader, from which every engine derives its
compile classpath. Runtime identity follows, since snippet loaders are children of the shared
loader. Compile-time visibility is the open question, because `dependenciesFromClassloader`
snapshots the classpath into a `JvmDependency(files)` rather than holding a live view of the
loader.

The spike runs three probes:

- **A**, the measurement: a directory that was on the classpath snapshot but empty at the time.
  Does a class file that appears in it later resolve in an engine that already exists? If it
  does, publishing a shared type is writing a file; if not, publishing has to rebuild the
  consuming engines.
- **B**, an invariant: a fresh engine sees the directory, the fallback the design rests on.
- **C**, an invariant: named arguments, `toString`, `copy` and destructuring of a `data class`
  work across the trip, which
  needs real Kotlin metadata rather than only a loadable JVM class.

It fails on B or C and reports A either way.

## SharedTypesSmokeTest.kt { #sharedtypessmoketest-kt }

End-to-end smoke for [`SharedTypes`](workspace.md#sharedtypes-kt-sharedtypes): publishing user-declared Kotlin types that every box can name.

The assertions cover the whole arc the feature exists for:

 - `testPublishProducesLoadableClasses` — publish compiles and lands on the shared loader.
 - `testPublishedTypeIsExportable` — the payoff for `@exported`. A published type passes
   [`ExportedTypeNames`](workspace.md#exportedtypenames-kt-exportedtypenames), so it crosses between boxes with its real type where a box-declared class
   can only ever cross as `Any?`. This is the join between the two halves of the work.
 - `testFreshEngineGetsFullFidelity` — named arguments, `copy`, destructuring and the data-class
   `toString` all survive, which only happens because these are real compiled classes.

`measureRepublish` is a measurement rather than an assertion, in the style of
`SharedTypesClasspathSpike`: it reports whether a *second* publish of the same class name actually
takes effect. It may well not — `gen-1` was added to the classloader before `gen-2`, and URL
search order is first-wins — and if so that is a real constraint on the feature, not a test bug.

## SpareEngines.kt { #spareengines-kt }

A box's next Kotlin engine, built while the box is idle.

Running a box gives it a fresh REPL, and building one costs a few hundred milliseconds that the
person who pressed the key waits through. [`SpareEngines`](workspace.md#spareengines-kt-spareengines) moves that wait off the keypress: once a
run has its verdict, the box's next engine is built on a background thread, and the next run
takes the one already standing by. The run still gets a fresh engine; only the waiting moves.

Engines are tens of megabytes, so only a handful of boxes hold one at a time, the least recently
prepared giving way first. A spare is dropped when its box is retired, and refused if the shared
class loader has gained jars since the spare was built, because an engine fixes its compile
classpath when it is created. `-Dafield.kotlin.spareEngines=0` turns the whole thing off.

## WitherSmokeTest.kt { #withersmoketest-kt }

Smoke for the experiment that wires the Wither compiler plugin (kyay10/wither) into the
K2 REPL ([`KotlinInterface2`](workspace.md#kotlininterface2-kt-kotlininterface2)). Wither is a FIR + IR plugin: a call to
`io.github.kyay10.wither.with(x)` turns `x` into an implicit receiver for the rest of the
enclosing block, and its IR pass rewrites the receiver-less member accesses that follow.

`testReceiverInjection` is the assertion that decides the run: a bare `greet()` with no explicit
receiver only resolves if Wither injected the `Greeter` receiver. Without the plugin the
snippet fails to compile (`unresolved reference 'greet'`), so a green run shows that the plugin
is registered into the REPL's compilation config and working end to end.

`testPlainEvalStillWorks` is the regression half: turning the plugin on must not disturb
ordinary snippet evaluation.

Runnable-object test style, matching [`ReplBootstrapGateTest`](workspace.md#replbootstrapgatetest-kt-replbootstrapgatetest).

### Red from 2026-08-25 to 2026-10-04: Wither's IR pass never recognised its own `with`

`testReceiverInjection` failed with an `IrErrorCallExpression` reaching codegen:

    Unresolved reference: this@R|<local>/<with holder>|
    AssertionError: Unexpected IR element found during code generation ... or it should have been lowered

fir2ir emitting that error call is expected. Wither's FIR half binds the injected receiver to a
synthetic holder that fir2ir cannot translate, and its IR half (`WitherReceiverTransformer`) exists
to patch it: it removes each `with(...)` statement, stores the argument in a temporary, and
replaces each `<with holder>` error call with a read of that temporary. The bug was that the pass
never matched the `with(...)` call. The IR dump in the failure still held

    CALL 'public final fun with (vararg values: kotlin.Any?): kotlin.Unit `companion` declared in io.github.kyay10.wither.WithKt'

The callee comes from `libs/wither-annotations.jar`, and in IR its parent is the JVM file facade
class, not the package fragment. A temporary probe in the pass printed `parent=IrClassImpl
parentOrigin=FILE_CLASS isTopLevel=true kotlinFqName=io.github.kyay10.wither`. Wither matched on
`callableId` against the package-level `CallableId(io.github.kyay10.wither, with)`; under a
facade class that id is `io/github/kyay10/wither/WithKt.with`, so the two were never equal. (Since
5052517 the pass refused any parent that was not a package fragment, which fails the same way.)
`~/temp/wither` `field/kotlin-2.5.0-beta1` @ face220 accepts both top-level shapes and compares
package plus name.

Measured 2026-10-04 on Kotlin 2.5.0-Beta1, same worktree and harness, changing only
`libs/wither-plugin.jar`:

 - the jar on `main` before the swap (sha1 `2869851…`): XFAIL, `with` CALL still in the IR, `got: null`;
 - 5052517 (`1e6f4c6…`): XFAIL, same IR, same `got: null`;
 - face220 (`be020c9…`): passes; `demo()` returns `hi-W`.

With face220, `kotlin.repl-snippet-declarations.smoke`, `kotlin.repl.provide-delegate` and
`kotlin.repl-local-fun-statements.box` also pass. Those runs used the versions of those tests that
expect 5052517's `has no callableId` fix.

Not measured: why the jar set from before the 2.4.20 uplift passed. The earlier diagnosis in this
KDoc blamed `Fir2IrVisitor.visitThisReceiverExpression` for producing the error call. That is true,
but fir2ir is supposed to produce it, as described above. Nobody checked how the older compiler
parented the callee.

When rebuilding the jar: `JAVA_HOME=<jdk-22> ./gradlew --configure-on-demand :compiler-plugin:jar`
in `~/temp/wither` (class file 66; the compiler host is a JDK 22). The build is reproducible, so
compare `shasum` with `libs/`.

## boxImports.kt { #boximports-kt }

Which of a box's imports it needs.

A box is compiled with the `intro` preamble prepended (`Boxes.kt`), so an import already provided
by that preamble adds nothing, and agents write such lines all the time. This reads a box's own
import lines and says, for each one, whether it is redundant (the intro already provides it),
unused (nothing in the code names it), needed, or kept because the evidence is not good enough to
drop it. `formatBoxImports` removes the first two kinds and sorts the rest; nothing here ever adds
an import.

The rules are conservative, because a wrongly dropped import is a compile error:

- An explicit import `a.b.C` (or `a.b.C as D`) is needed when its name appears as an identifier in
  the code, outside comments and strings. Operator-convention names (`plusAssign`, `getValue`,
  `invoke`, ...) are always kept: code uses them without writing them.
- It is redundant when the intro has the same line, or `a.b.*` and no other visible package
  (including Kotlin/JVM defaults) offers a competing `C`. An aliased import is never redundant.
- A star import `a.b.*` is redundant when the intro has the same star. It is unused only on the
  evidence `k2ImportEvidence` collects: K2 resolved every reference in the box and none of them
  lives in `a.b`. Without that evidence a star import is kept.

## formatter.kt { #formatter-kt }

Reformats a box's Kotlin or GLSL code.

[`formatCodeProperty`](workspace.md#formatter-kt--formatcodeproperty) picks the formatter by property name: [`formatKotlinCode`](workspace.md#formatter-kt--formatkotlincode) for `code`, which runs
ktfmt and then restores Field-specific layout such as fragment breaks and comment blocks, and
[`formatGlslCode`](workspace.md#formatter-kt--formatglslcode) for shader properties.

## importHelp.kt { #importhelp-kt }

Finds which classes a bare name could mean, so Field can write the `import` line for it.

A class-path index, built once by [`initializeClassCache`](workspace.md#importhelp-kt--initializeclasscache), maps simple class names to fully
qualified ones. [`findClassesNamed`](workspace.md#importhelp-kt--findclassesnamed), [`classesWithPrefix`](workspace.md#importhelp-kt--classeswithprefix) and [`kotlinImportStatementFor`](workspace.md#importhelp-kt--kotlinimportstatementfor) answer
completion and auto-import from it, filtered by the user's import blacklist. [`ImportResolution`](workspace.md#importhelp-kt-importresolution)
controls whether that answer depends on the local machine.

## LanguageRoots.kt { #languageroots-kt }

The roots of the small languages that draw in a window — RectSL and StackSL — made and given a
window by the language, so that starting one takes a command rather than Kotlin.

[`adopt`](workspace.md#languageroots-kt--languageroots--adopt) is "Make a RectSL Scene" and "Make a StackSL Program": the selected box goes beneath a root of
that language — the one already above it, or a new one placed just above it — and becomes a scene.

A box marked "Set Main Language: RectSL" (or StackSL) is the root its scenes draw beneath. When a
scene starts and there is no running window above it, [`ensure`](workspace.md#languageroots-kt--languageroots--ensure) opens one on that root — a `Window`
and a `Renderer` held in the root's `window` and `renderer` properties, exactly where
`prop<Renderer>(renderer)` would have put them, with the render loop running as the root's job. So the
root shows as running, stopping it closes the window (and, as for any renderer box, stops the scenes
drawing in it first), and closing the window stops them too; running a scene again reopens it.

A root that holds Kotlin of its own is left to open its own window: that Kotlin may be about to, and
two render loops on one renderer would fight. [`ensure`](workspace.md#languageroots-kt--languageroots--ensure) only says so.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/languages/LanguageRoots.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/languages/LanguageRoots/)

## LanguageSpecs.kt { #languagespecs-kt }

The text conventions of the languages a box property can hold: each [`LanguageSpec`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt-languagespec) says how to wrap
a property's source before it is compiled and how to unwrap it again.

Kotlin box code is wrapped by [`wrapScript`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt--wrapscript) into a `fun SCRIPT()` block between preamble and
postamble markers, keeping leading `import` and `@file` lines above it, and [`unwrapScriptLenient`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt--unwrapscriptlenient)
takes it back out. GLSL specs normalise the preamble to `#version 450` followed by the source's
`#extension` lines; the ray-tracing stages use `#version 460` and always add `GL_EXT_ray_tracing`.
Slang specs only trim trailing whitespace.

[`glslSpecForProperty`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt--glslspecforproperty) and [`shaderSpecForProperty`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt--shaderspecforproperty) map a property name to its spec, case-insensitively:
`vertex`, `fragment`, `mesh`, `task`, `compute` and the ray-tracing stages (`raygen`, `miss`,
`closesthit`, `anyhit`, `intersection`, `callable`) are GLSL, and the same names with an `_s` suffix,
plus `vertex_fragment`, are Slang. [`NANO_ASM`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt--nano-asm) is the spec for the Nano assembly language.

| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--enabled"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enabled</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L71) | Whether newly compiled box code polls, and whether the [`Watchdog`](workspace.md#boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--watchdog) may interrupt. Off, the watchdog still reports stalls. Code compiled while it was on stays interruptible until it is recompiled. |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--applypreference"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">applyPreference</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">on</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L74) | Apply the persisted preference (`FieldPreferences.boxInterrupt`), unless the env/property override is set. |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--poll"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">poll</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L86) | Called by instrumented box code at every method entry and loop back-edge. Must stay cheap: the common path is one opaque read and a null check. Opaque, not volatile: a volatile read on every back-edge is an acquire barrier that stops the JIT vectorising the loop (`a[`i`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt--i) += i` over an `IntArray` ran ~20x slower), while an opaque read still cannot be hoisted out of the loop, so a request is seen within an iteration or two. The compare-and-set below is the real fence. |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--request"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">request</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">reason</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">thread</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Thread</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Runloop</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">mainThread</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L107) | Ask `thread` (by default the Runloop thread) to leave box code at its next poll. Returns false when there is no such thread. Safe to call from any thread, including while the Runloop is blocked. A request is withdrawn by the [`Watchdog`](workspace.md#boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--watchdog) once the Runloop makes progress again, so a request that found no box code to land in cannot fire later in an unrelated box. |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--ispending"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">isPending</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L124) | True while a request has not yet landed or been withdrawn. |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--culprit"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">culprit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">stack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Array</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">StackTraceElement</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L132) | Box label that owns the innermost snippet frame in `stack`, or null. |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--instrument"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">instrument</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">script</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CompiledScript</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">boxLabel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L144) | Rewrite the newest snippet of `script` so its code polls. Idempotent per compiled module; a module of an unknown shape is left alone (and logged once). |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--instrumentclass"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">instrumentClass</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bytes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ByteArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">boxLabel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ByteArray</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L168) | `bytes` rewritten to poll, recording its class as `boxLabel`'s; null if it is not rewritable (then the class runs unchanged, just not interruptibly). |
| <a id="boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--watchdog"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Watchdog</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/BoxInterrupt/#L237) | Notices that [`Runloop.frame`](workspace.md#runloop-kt--runloop--frame) has stopped advancing. After `reportAfterMs` it logs the stall once, with the culprit box and the Runloop thread's stack; after `interruptAfterMs` (0 = never) it [`request`](workspace.md#boxinterrupt-kt--boxinterrupt--request)s an interrupt. Runs on its own daemon thread; never touches Runloop state beyond reading the frame counter and the thread's stack. |

## LifecycleLedger.kt { #lifecycleledger-kt }

The ledger of everything a box has registered with a longer-lived subsystem, and the handles that release it.

Audio patches, control callbacks, Runloop hooks, render modules and feeder threads are each claimed
as an [`Ownership`](workspace.md#lifecycleledger-kt-ownership) through [`LifecycleLedger`](workspace.md#lifecycleledger-kt-lifecycleledger), tagged with the box executing at the time. The run
scopes in `RunScope.kt` decide when each one is released; [`lifecycleCensus`](workspace.md#lifecycleledger-kt--lifecyclecensus) counts what is still
live per box, which is how a test checks that a stopped or retired box left nothing behind.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/lifecycle/LifecycleLedger.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/LifecycleLedger/)

## Phased.kt { #phased-kt }

Frame-by-frame animation for box code: return a [`Frames`](workspace.md#phased-kt-frames) and Field runs it once per Runloop frame.

[`frames`](workspace.md#phased-kt--frames), [`eachFrame`](workspace.md#phased-kt--eachframe), [`loop`](workspace.md#phased-kt--loop) and [`forever`](workspace.md#phased-kt--forever) build a [`Frames`](workspace.md#phased-kt-frames) from a suspending body that calls
`frame()` to wait for the next frame; [`Box.launchFrames`](workspace.md#phased-kt--launchframes) runs one on the [`Framer`](workspace.md#phased-kt-framer) dispatcher. The
file also holds [`Generator`](workspace.md#phased-kt-generator), a small coroutine-based generator built with [`generator`](workspace.md#phased-kt--generator) or
[`generator2`](workspace.md#phased-kt--generator2).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/lifecycle/Phased.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/Phased/)

## ReactiveRuns.kt { #reactiveruns-kt }

Reactive properties: the runs that `propUp` pulls from upstream and `propDown` pushes downstream.

A read that finds no value runs the box that supplies it before returning; a write that changes a
value reruns the boxes that read the old one. [`ReactiveRuns`](workspace.md#reactiveruns-kt-reactiveruns) holds both mechanisms and their
guards.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/lifecycle/ReactiveRuns.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/ReactiveRuns/)

## RunScope.kt { #runscope-kt }

Run scopes: what a box's run owns, and which of stop, re-run or retire releases it.

Each run of a box gets a [`RunScope`](workspace.md#runscope-kt-runscope); registrations made while it executes are owned by that scope
and carry a [`ReleasePolicy`](workspace.md#runscope-kt-releasepolicy). [`BoxRunScopes`](workspace.md#runscope-kt-boxrunscopes) holds a box's scopes, so a re-run supersedes the last
run's scope, a stop releases only what is running, and retiring the box releases everything.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/lifecycle/RunScope.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/RunScope/)

**Used in:** [Beat and pitch analysis](../audio_ai_analysis.md), [Corpus microscope: from recordings to related windows](../audio_ai_corpus_microscope.md), [Short-time spectral spaces](../audio_ai_spectral_embeddings.md)

## Runloop.kt { #runloop-kt }

The main Field loop: [`Runloop`](workspace.md#runloop-kt-runloop) ticks `preRun`, the [`Framer`](workspace.md#phased-kt-framer) dispatcher and `postRun` once per frame on one thread.

`Runloop.runLoop` is the single instance and [`Runloop.frame`](workspace.md#runloop-kt--runloop--frame) its frame counter. [`inMain`](workspace.md#runloop-kt--inmain) launches a
coroutine onto that loop, `Runloop.miscPool` is the shared pool for background work, and
[`AnimationClock`](workspace.md#runloop-kt-animationclock) is the time source that frame-based code reads, which becomes frame-indexed during
a frame-synchronous video capture. [`RateLimiter`](workspace.md#runloop-kt-ratelimiter) coalesces bursts of work to a fixed rate. The
Runloop is not the audio thread; see `FieldAudioEngine` for that.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/lifecycle/Runloop.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/Runloop/)

## SimulationClock.kt { #simulationclock-kt }

A manually stepped coroutine clock, so `delay` and `withTimeout` inside a box follow simulation time.

[`withSimulationClock`](workspace.md#simulationclock-kt--withsimulationclock) opens a [`SimulationClock`](workspace.md#simulationclock-kt-simulationclock) inside ordinary [`frames`](workspace.md#phased-kt--frames) code; each [`SimulationClock.advance`](workspace.md#simulationclock-kt--simulationclock--advance)
moves simulation time forward and resumes the coroutines that are due, within a resume budget.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">SimulationClock</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">parentContext</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CoroutineContext</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stepSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span> <span class="p">/</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxStepsPerAdvance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxResumesPerStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1024</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CoroutineScope</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/SimulationClock/#L53)

A coroutine scope with a manually stepped dispatcher. It creates no thread and registers no new box launcher. Use [`withSimulationClock`](workspace.md#simulationclock-kt--withsimulationclock) inside ordinary [`frames`](workspace.md#phased-kt--frames); standard `launch` children inherit the box, source and parent job. `delay` and `withTimeout` then use simulation time. [`advance`](workspace.md#simulationclock-kt--simulationclock--advance) and [`close`](workspace.md#simulationclock-kt--simulationclock--close) belong to the creating thread; dispatch and cancellation may enqueue from another thread.

## di.kt { #di-kt }

Startup phases: functions annotated [`RunsAt`](workspace.md#di-kt-runsat) are found by a classpath scan and called by [`runAll`](workspace.md#di-kt--runall) at a named phase.

The phase names are the constants at the top of this file ([`early`](workspace.md#di-kt--early), [`plugins`](workspace.md#di-kt--plugins), [`installHandlers`](workspace.md#di-kt--installhandlers),
[`newRoot`](workspace.md#di-kt--newroot), ...). [`runAll`](workspace.md#di-kt--runall) calls every function registered for a phase in priority order, passing
those arguments its parameters ask for. The same scan fills [`labelledArgumentFunctions`](workspace.md#di-kt--labelledargumentfunctions).

## util_lifecycle.kt { #util-lifecycle-kt }

[`LazyVar`](workspace.md#util-lifecycle-kt-lazyvar), a lazy value that can also be assigned, and its [`lazyVar`](workspace.md#util-lifecycle-kt--lazyvar) factory.

Assigning the value before the first read means its initializer never runs, and [`LazyVar.discard`](workspace.md#util-lifecycle-kt--lazyvar--discard)
forgets the value so the next read builds it again. A value that is dropped without being
cached goes to an `onDiscard` callback, so something that needs releasing is released once.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/runtime/lifecycle/util_lifecycle.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/util_lifecycle/)

## PatternRewrite.kt { #patternrewrite-kt }

Pattern-based rewrite rules for box code, written in the box itself with a `rewrite { from { } to { } }`
block and applied to the source before it compiles.

The rules are matched on the parsed syntax tree, not on text, so `from { max(x, y) }` matches any
call of `max` with two arguments whatever their spelling. [`PatternRewrite`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt-patternrewrite) describes the phases,
guards and hygiene rules.

## RewriteDsl.kt { #rewritedsl-kt }

The rule-authoring surface for the pattern-rewrite layer (see [`PatternRewrite`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt-patternrewrite)).

These declarations are *erased*: a `rewrite { … }` block is collected and deleted from the
source by [`PatternRewrite.expand`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt--patternrewrite--expand) **before** the K2 REPL ever compiles it, so none of these
functions is ever actually called at run time. They exist only so a rule authored in a live box
  - parses,
  - is importable (`import afield.runtime.macros.*`), and
  - reads sensibly (the names `rewrite` / `from` / `to` / `Expr` resolve to something).

The whole point (see [`PatternRewrite`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt-patternrewrite)) is that a rule body never needs to *type-check* — only
parse. PSI parsing runs no name resolution, so `from { max(x, y) }` parses into a valid tree even
though `max`, `x`, `y` resolve to nothing. If one of these functions is somehow reached at run
time it means expansion did not happen, which is a bug — hence the throw.

Surface:
```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
rewrite { x: Expr, y: Expr ->
    from { max(x, y) }
    to   { if (x >= y) x else y }
}
```
The lambda's value parameters (`x: Expr, y: Expr`) are the metavariable declarations: inside
`from`/`to`, a name reference is a hole iff its name is in that parameter set, and its declared
type names the [`MetaKind`](workspace.md#rewritedsl-kt-metakind). No `unquote`/`$`/`,` escape is needed — the known metavar set *is* the
escape.

## ai_macro.kt { #ai-macro-kt }

The `ai("...")` macro, which asks a language model to write the body of the function it is called
in and caches the result in the box's attic.

The containing function must declare its parameter types and return type; the signature and the
prompt go to the model through [`AiMacroBridge`](workspace.md#ai-macro-kt-aimacrobridge), and the generated function is stored between
`// @ai-gen:` and `// @ai-gen-end:` comment lines so it is reused rather than regenerated
([`parseAtticBlock`](workspace.md#ai-macro-kt--parseatticblock), [`appendAtticBlock`](workspace.md#ai-macro-kt--appendatticblock), [`removeAtticBlock`](workspace.md#ai-macro-kt--removeatticblock)). [`resolvePatternRewriteAi`](workspace.md#ai-macro-kt--resolvepatternrewriteai) serves the
`ai(...)` side contributions of [`PatternRewrite`](workspace.md#patternrewrite-kt-patternrewrite) rules through the same cache.

## macros.kt { #macros-kt }

The call-rewriting macro pass that box code goes through before it compiles: a call such as
`prop(...)`, `moduleHere(...)` or `_println(...)` is replaced by source text generated for the box
that contains it.

[`MacroRegistry`](workspace.md#macros-kt-macroregistry) maps a call name to its rewrite and returns an [`Insert`](workspace.md#macros-kt-insert) describing the replacement.
The rest of the file supports that pass: gathering the preamble a box inherits from its parents
([`gatherPreambleUpwards`](workspace.md#macros-kt--gatherpreambleupwards), with conflicts reported by [`gatherPreambleUpwardsReport`](workspace.md#macros-kt--gatherpreambleupwardsreport)), tagging
preamble lines with the uid of the box that supplied them, and splitting a box at `//%-` fragment
breaks ([`isFragmentBreak`](workspace.md#macros-kt--isfragmentbreak), [`fragmentBreakIndices`](workspace.md#macros-kt--fragmentbreakindices)) so that compiler diagnostics can be moved back
to the right line ([`rebaseFragmentDiagnostics`](workspace.md#macros-kt--rebasefragmentdiagnostics)).

## BoxStudyBuilds.kt { #boxstudybuilds-kt }

The box surface for study builds: [`Box.studyBuilds`](workspace.md#boxstudybuilds-kt--studybuilds) attaches a named [`StudyBuilds`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuilds) runner to a box,
and [`Box.showStudyBuilds`](workspace.md#boxstudybuilds-kt--showstudybuilds) shows its stage buttons, progress and diagnostics in an output channel.

The runner keeps its history under the document's `studies` directory, is replaced when the box
runs again, and closes when the box stops. Runners on boxes of the same document can depend on each
other's stages through `dependsOn(runner, stage)`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/build/BoxStudyBuilds.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/build/BoxStudyBuilds/)

## StudyBuildHelpers.kt { #studybuildhelpers-kt }

Helpers a [`StudyBuildStage`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuildstage) uses to name what it runs: [`fileIdentity`](workspace.md#studybuildhelpers-kt--fileidentity) and [`classIdentity`](workspace.md#studybuildhelpers-kt--classidentity) hash the
source files or compiled classes behind a build, for its `recipeVersion` or an input, so results go
stale when that code changes.

[`StudyBuildProcessResult`](workspace.md#studybuildhelpers-kt-studybuildprocessresult) is what a stage's external process reported: exit code, retained log and
last progress message.

## StudyBuilds.kt { #studybuilds-kt }

Durable derived builds for a study: named stages whose results are fingerprinted against their
inputs and recipe, kept on disk with their attempt history, and reported stale when either changes.

A [`StudyBuildStage`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuildstage) declares an id, a `recipeVersion`, the input keys it reads and the stages it
depends on; [`StudyBuilds`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuilds) runs those stages on worker threads under a directory it owns through a
file lock. A [`StudyBuildGate`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuildgate) adds an input that exists only while a check passes, and
`dependsOn(runner, stage)` names a stage of another runner in the same document. Reading
[`StudyBuilds.stages`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuilds--stages) recomputes currency, [`StudyBuilds.start`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuilds--start) and [`StudyBuilds.cancel`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuilds--cancel) drive one
attempt, and [`StudyBuilds.prune`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuilds--prune) deletes attempts that no current result, running build or pin needs. From a box, attach a
runner with [`Box.studyBuilds`](workspace.md#boxstudybuilds-kt--studybuilds) (`BoxStudyBuilds.kt`).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/build/StudyBuilds.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/build/StudyBuilds/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md), [Let AI4 Wait for Long Builds](../ai4_long_builds.md)

Only [`box`](workspace.md#boxes-kt--box) and `caption` are reported in tool results.

class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/build/StudyBuilds/#L183)

A reusable build stage. [`inputKeys`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuildstage--inputkeys) selects only the authored inputs this stage consumes, and may name [`StudyBuildGate`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuildgate)s; `dependencies` names other stages whose current results must exist first, either in this runner or, written `dependsOn(runner, stage)`, in another runner of the same document. `recipeVersion` must change when the adapter or its relevant runtime changes. The runner does not infer code identity from a closure. `inputHelp` explains missing inputs without making the stage runnable or changing its fingerprint; a closed gate supplies its own explanation. `resultNotes` is a fast, pure presentation of a completed record's retained facts; it must not inspect mutable design state or change acceptance. It is shared by UI and agent tools and does not change build identity. Qualification gates belong in the build and input contracts. `failureNotes` is the same presentation for a FAILED record, usually over its [`StudyBuildRecord.problem`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuildrecord--problem) details, under the same rules; it is opt-in, and its notes, views included, appear wherever result notes would. A failed record is never current: its notes appear beside the failure, never as the current result's. [`build`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt--studybuildstage--build) runs on a worker and must use its captured context, not mutable live input.

## StudyEvidence.kt { #studyevidence-kt }

Measures and lays out the frames a study renders: brightness, clipping, non-finite pixels, detail,
palette, frame-to-frame motion and region-restricted differences, plus labelled contact sheets of
tiles for a model to look at.

[`StudyEvidence`](workspace.md#studyevidence-kt-studyevidence) holds the functions; [`StudyFrameStats`](workspace.md#studyevidence-kt-studyframestats), [`StudyMotion`](workspace.md#studyevidence-kt-studymotion) and [`StudyDifference`](workspace.md#studyevidence-kt-studydifference) are the
numbers it returns. Measurements are taken from the program's raw output before the display clamp,
so clipping is counted rather than hidden.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/evidence/StudyEvidence.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/evidence/StudyEvidence/)

### StudyFrameStats { #studyevidence-kt-studyframestats }

## StudyVariants.kt { #studyvariants-kt }

The parts of a live study's variant search that do not depend on what the study draws.

[`StudyVariants`](workspace.md#studyvariants-kt-studyvariants) holds the candidates a study has tried, on disk under `speculations/`, until one is
adopted, and picks the newest unadopted batch back up after a restart. [`StudyCompare`](workspace.md#studyvariants-kt-studycompare) does the
picture side of *Compare* and *Sweep*: before | after | difference tiles with a check that nothing
changed outside the allowed region, and a sweep that draws 2 to 9 values of one parameter.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/search/StudyVariants.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/search/StudyVariants/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md)

## LiveStudy.kt { #livestudy-kt }

The standard study verbs, and the tools that offer them to an AI4 agent: inspect, edit, patch, set
numbers, observe, compare, sweep, try variants, adopt a variant and restore a revision.

[`LiveStudy`](workspace.md#livestudy-kt-livestudy) is the interface a study implements. [`StudyRequest`](workspace.md#livestudy-kt-studyrequest) holds the request shapes the verbs
take, which a library study's own request classes implement; [`registerStudyTools`](workspace.md#livestudy-kt--registerstudytools) wires those
classes to a study once. From box code, [`Box.registerStudyTools`](workspace.md#livestudy-kt--registerstudytools) makes the same verbs as
box-authored tools named after a prefix, using the [`StudyCall`](workspace.md#livestudy-kt-studycall) request classes.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/LiveStudy.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/LiveStudy/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md)

| --- | --- |

A study registers its extras (a guide, a trace, an export) itself. |

A library study adapts its own class to it; a document can implement it directly, or use [`SourceFramesStudy`](workspace.md#sourceframesstudy-kt-sourceframesstudy), which implements all of it from the shared pieces. A verb a study does not offer refuses with a message saying so.

## QualifiedSource.kt { #qualifiedsource-kt }

### Qualified sources: changing a rule without breaking what already works

A rule (a placement recipe, a fallback, a solver strategy) is a source that other builds consume.
A [`QualifiedSource`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedsource) keeps three things beside it and lets the rule change only when all three agree:

- the **rule**, a [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy) over a box property;
- the **fixtures**, a [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy) of retained real cases, each an exact input and the outcome the rule
  gave it ([`QualifiedFixture`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedfixture));
- a **replay** stage, a [`StudyBuilds`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuilds) runner that runs a candidate rule on every fixture and on a
  [`QualifiedControl`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcontrol), an input no correct rule can pass, which must fail.

A change starts as a *candidate*: a frozen record of the base it was made against, its source, the
fixtures, the dependencies and the checks ([`QualifiedCandidate`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcandidate)), named by the hash of all of them. The
replay compares each fixture's new outcome with the recorded one: the same, changed, or held (the rule
or its checks refused it). A candidate is admitted, and `apply` publishes it through
[`SourceStudy.edit`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt--sourcestudy--edit), only when its replay is current, covers every fixture with the same outcome, the
control failed as it must, and nothing it depends on has changed.

The checks that judge a candidate are out of its reach ([`FrozenRegion`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-frozenregion)): files it may not edit, text
after a marker that must stay byte for byte, or a separate frozen copy. Only a person changes them, and
only a person changes a fixture's recorded outcome: `proposeRebaseline` draws each changed outcome with
an **Approve** button, and the press records who approved it and when. No tool approves.

[`Box.qualifiedSource`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt--qualifiedsource) makes one in a box and registers the agent tools `<name>.inspect`, `.candidate`,
`.test`, `.apply`, `.retainFixture` and `.proposeRebaseline`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/)
