### QualifiedControl { #qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcontrol }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">QualifiedControl</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">messageContains</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L134)

An input no correct rule can pass, replayed with every candidate. Its replay must fail (the rule or its checks throw), with `messageContains` in the message when given. A control that passes means the checks are not running, so no candidate is admitted.

### FrozenRegion { #qualifiedsource-kt-frozenregion }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FrozenRegion</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L143)

Where a qualified source keeps its checks out of a candidate's reach. A candidate breaking any of its regions is refused before it is saved. What the regions freeze is recorded in the candidate as `QualifiedCandidate.checks` and handed to the replay as `QualifiedReplay.checks`.

## SourceFramesStudy.kt { #sourceframesstudy-kt }

A complete study for any text that draws, so a document can offer an agent the standard study verbs
without writing a study class.

[`SourceFramesStudy`](workspace.md#sourceframesstudy-kt-sourceframesstudy) keeps revisions of the source, draws frames through a [`StudyFrames`](workspace.md#studyframes-kt-studyframes), and
answers every [`LiveStudy`](workspace.md#livestudy-kt-livestudy) verb. [`Box.sourceFramesStudy`](workspace.md#sourceframesstudy-kt--sourceframesstudy) builds one for a box property,
[`studyFrames`](workspace.md#sourceframesstudy-kt--studyframes) turns a single-frame drawing function into a [`StudyFrames`](workspace.md#studyframes-kt-studyframes), and [`StudyKnobs`](workspace.md#sourceframesstudy-kt-studyknobs) finds
and rewrites the plainly written numbers in a source.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/SourceFramesStudy.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/SourceFramesStudy/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md)

## SourceStudy.kt { #sourcestudy-kt }

The language-neutral half of a live-code study: the part of "talking a function into existence"
that does not care what the language is.

A study holds one editable source — the text in a box that a person and a model are both working
on — and a durable, append-only history of the versions of it that passed a check. Every change
arrives as a *transaction*: the caller names the revision it read and a hash of the live source it
read, the candidate is checked by the language adapter, and only then is it written into the box,
with a compare-and-swap against the text that is there *now*. So a model preparing an edit while a
person types cannot overwrite the person, a candidate that fails its check changes nothing, and
every accepted version can be read back, compared and restored.

What the language adds is one function, [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy)'s `admit`: compile and check a candidate,
returning a value (whatever the language's tools need — a composition, a compiled shader report)
or throwing [`StudyRejection`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-studyrejection) with a message a person or a model can act on. The StackSL, RectSL,
stack.auto and function studies are all adapters over it; `FunctionStudy` predated it and kept a
private copy of the protocol until 2026-09-29, with the same file layout, so a revision directory
written before then still reads.

### On disk

`directory/<id>.<extension>` is a revision's source and `directory/<id>.json` its metadata (parent,
description, time, and whatever facts the adapter chose to keep). `directory/HEAD` names the checked
revision the box last held. An id is `r<n>-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(source)>`, so an id also
verifies its own file: a revision whose source was edited on disk refuses to load.

This is trusted local code, not a sandbox: `admit` runs whatever the adapter runs. Cancellation
([`cancel`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt--sourcestudy--cancel)) stops a pending publication, not a computation that never checks for it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/SourceStudy.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/SourceStudy/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md)

## StudyKeys.kt { #studykeys-kt }

Keys for a study card: a snapshot of every number in a program, saved by name, which the card can
apply or blend towards. They are the person's way of keeping "this look" and "that look" and moving
between them before choosing a revision.

A key is a [`KeyframeScope`](graphics.md#keyframer-kt-keyframescope) key like any other, saved with [`KeyframeScope.saveKey`](graphics.md#keyframer-kt--keyframescope--savekey), so each has its
`.versions` history and the keyframe browser can read the folder. Its values are the knobs by index
(`k0`, `k1`, …) and, under `shape`, the shape of the program it came from: that program's text with
every number blanked out, the language, and what reads each number. So a key applies to the program
it was captured from, and to that program with any of its numbers changed, but not to one whose text
has changed around them, where the same index may be a different number.

Keys live in `keys/` in the study's directory.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/StudyKeys.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/StudyKeys/)

## sourceBlock.kt { #sourceblock-kt }

A block of code that is also its own source: call it like a function, and it carries the Kotlin
text it was written as.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val answer = sourceBlock { 6 * 7 }
println(answer())          // 42
println(answer.source)     // 6 * 7
```

A macro: before the box compiles, `sourceBlock { … }` is rewritten to a [`SourceBackedBlock`](internal.md#sourcebackedblock-kt-sourcebackedblock) holding
both the live lambda and the text of its body. Code that saves a block (a keyframe track, a
code-blend plan) saves that text, and a block loaded back from it compiles the text again, in the
box it came from, the first time it is called. So a saved block works before (or without) the box
that wrote it running again.

A block made by this call carries its lambda and is safe to call at once. A block loaded back from
saved text is not safe to call from inside its own box's running code: compiling it runs that box's
code again, which calls the block again. Call it from another box, a frame loop or a control
callback; [`SourceBackedBlockSelfBoxReentry`](internal.md#sourcebackedblock-kt-sourcebackedblockselfboxreentry) stops the loop and says so if you do.

Should the macro not run (code that reaches this function some other way), the result still works,
with an empty [`SourceBackedBlock.source`](internal.md#sourcebackedblock-kt--sourcebackedblock--source).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/sourceBlock.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/sourceBlock/)

## KnobNames.kt { #knobnames-kt }

Short names for the numbers of a program, like `wave drift speed` or `star brightness`, for the
sliders of a study card, written by Field's fast model from what the compiler already knows.

A card can always say what reads a number: StackSL's compiler records what took it (`mix amount`,
`x of palette a`), RectSL's tokens the word that reads it (`->wall width`). That is exact, but a
program whose numbers mostly scale and offset reads as a column of `multiplies` and `adds`. So the
card shows that at first, and asks the fast model once, for all of the program's numbers at a time,
to say in a few words what turning each one changes, given the program with its comments and each
number's line, spelling and operand. The compiler's label stays on the slider's tooltip.

Names are kept by the program's shape: its text with every number blanked out, the language, and
what reads each number. Turning a number, or keeping one, never asks again; the names are stored in
the study's directory, beside its revisions, so a document carries them. Nothing is asked for a box
in no open document (a test's box), nor for a document an agent opened unless
`AFIELD_AI_KNOB_NAMES=1`; `0` turns asking off, and names already stored are still shown.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/ui/KnobNames.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/ui/KnobNames/)

## StudyKnob.kt { #studyknob-kt }

The language-neutral view of the numbers in a study's source: [`StudyKnob`](workspace.md#studyknob-kt-studyknob) describes one typed
number, and [`setNumbers`](workspace.md#studyknob-kt--setnumbers) applies a batch of new values, keyed by knob index, as a new
[`SourceRevision`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcerevision).

Each study language finds its own knobs and maps them to [`StudyKnob`](workspace.md#studyknob-kt-studyknob); slider naming (`KnobNames`)
and saved card keys (`StudyKeys`) work from that shared shape. [`setNumbers`](workspace.md#studyknob-kt--setnumbers) refuses an empty
request, a stale revision or source hash, and any value the language's rewriter rejects, each as a
[`StudyRejection`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-studyrejection).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/ui/StudyKnob.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/ui/StudyKnob/)

## AgentWorktreeManager.kt { #agentworktreemanager-kt }

Creates, lists, merges and deletes git worktrees that agents work in, one branch per proposal.

[`AgentWorktreeManager.createProposal`](workspace.md#agentworktreemanager-kt--agentworktreemanager--createproposal) adds a worktree on a new `agent/<task>/<id>` branch from the
current `HEAD` and records it as JSON in a `.metadata` folder under the worktree root. That root
is `afield.agentWorktreeRoot`, `AFIELD_AGENT_WORKTREE_ROOT`, or `<checkout>-agent-worktrees`
beside the checkout. `mergeProposal` refuses to merge into a checkout with uncommitted changes.

## MacroReplayCode.kt { #macroreplaycode-kt }

The code a replayed `execute` / `launch` op runs, and where in the box it sits.

A macro replays against the document as it is now, not as it was when the macro was recorded:

- A whole-box launch (`type: launch`, `code` or `all`) runs the box's current text. Any
  `code:` or `recordedCode:` on the op is a reference to what ran at recording time; a recording
  made before the box's code was edited still launches the edited code.
- A fragment (`type: fragment`, the default for `execute`, `execute-fragment` and
  `launch-fragment`) with an explicit `code:` runs that code: an authored transcript uses it to
  run a snippet that is not in the box. A recorded fragment carries `recordedCode:` instead and
  is found again in the box's current text — the same text where it still occurs (nearest its
  recorded line), otherwise the same lines of the current text.
- `codeSource: recorded` runs the op's own `code:` / `recordedCode:` as written, for a macro
  that has to replay exactly what ran.
- An op with no code at all runs the box's current text.

`note` says when what runs differs from what was recorded, for the replay log.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/automation/MacroReplayCode.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/automation/MacroReplayCode/)

## operation_transcript.kt { #operation-transcript-kt }

Records the operations a person or agent performs on a document and replays them as named macros.

[`OperationTranscript`](workspace.md#operation-transcript-kt-operationtranscript) logs edits, moves, executions, launches and stops as they happen
(`recordEdit`, `recordMove`, `recordExecuteFragment`, `recordLaunch`, `recordStop`), and stores
macros as YAML files in a `macros/` folder at document, project or workspace scope
(`listMacros`, `writeMacro`, `runMacro`). The backdoor's `macro write` and `macro run` commands
use this; the YAML format and examples are in `dev_docs/agents/OPERATION_TRANSCRIPT.md`.

## transcript.kt { #transcript-kt }

Keeps a per-document log of what ran in each box, for activity summaries and the transcript view.

[`FlightRecorder`](workspace.md#transcript-kt-flightrecorder) appends an entry for every execute, launch and stop, and for changes to tracked
box properties, then reports per-box execution and launch counts (`activitySummaryForDocument`,
stamped with the current Field launch id), per-line activity (`lineActivityForDocument`) and an HTML
rendering of the log (`htmlForDocument`). Older logs are kept as `transcript_backup_*.edn`
files in the document's `backups/` folder.

## AgentDemoDriftGuard.kt { #agentdemodriftguard-kt }

Checks that each loadable document under `dev_docs/agents/demos/` agrees with the loose source
files beside it.

A `#afield/file-inline` property has two copies: the fallback embedded in `metadata.edn`, and the
loose file beside it. Field prefers the loose file, so an edited demo can run correctly while the
metadata that is supposed to be canonical stays stale. This guard compares the two
byte-for-byte. `--write` refreshes the inline fallbacks through the EDN codec in [`SavingContext`](workspace.md#saving-kt-savingcontext).

`--write` rewrites `metadata.edn` for every document it visits, and re-encoding is not always
byte-identical to what is committed — a hand-edited artifact can carry `\uXXXX` escapes that the
codec re-emits as the literal character. That turns "add one demo" into a diff against unrelated
documents, which is an invitation to a merge conflict between two branches that each added one.
`--only <document>[,<document>…]` narrows the run to the documents named after the directory
under `dev_docs/agents/demos`, so adding a demo touches that demo alone.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/AgentDemoDriftGuard.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/AgentDemoDriftGuard/)

## AgentTranscriptIndexGuard.kt { #agenttranscriptindexguard-kt }

Fails the build when `public/docs/agent_transcripts.md` stops being a true index of
`dev_docs/agents/transcripts/`.

### The failure this exists to stop

The page calls itself "the illustrated index" of the transcript corpus and is the public front door
to Field's agent-automation story. The generated half of the same system cannot drift:
`AgentTranscriptMaterializer` and `checkAgentTranscripts` guard the committed starting-point bundle
byte-for-byte. The hand-curated page beside it has no such guard of its own, and goes stale the
moment anybody adds a transcript without remembering the page exists — a page that claims to list
every transcript, listing most of them.

The page is **not** generated, because its entries quote the number a box prints and say why that
number is the interesting one — `0.985 forwards, 0.246 backwards on a parabola`; `473 diagonal
breaks against 0`. None of that is in the yaml, which carries op verbs, box ids, rects and Kotlin
source; a generator over it could emit a name and a box count, which would replace the writing with
a table. So the trade here is [`KDocAttachmentGuard`](workspace.md#kdocattachmentguard-kt-kdocattachmentguard)'s, not [`StdlibReferenceGenerator`](workspace.md#stdlibreferencegenerator-kt-stdlibreferencegenerator)'s: keep the
prose hand-written and make its *incompleteness* a build failure, so a new transcript cannot ship
without somebody writing a sentence about it.

### The five things it checks

1. **Completeness** — every `*.yaml` in the corpus has exactly one entry. An entry is a `###`
   heading whose whole text is the transcript's name, `### transcript_name`, at column zero. `###`
   on that page is therefore reserved for entries: a sub-heading inside an entry has to be `####`
   or deeper, and a `###` naming anything else is read as an entry for a transcript that does not
   exist. A heading per entry is also what makes a hundred-odd scenes something a reader can link
   to and scroll through one at a time.
2. **No orphans** — every entry names a transcript that is still in the corpus, so deleting or
   renaming a yaml turns the stale paragraph red instead of leaving it to be read as current.
3. **The CI claim, per entry** — each `##` section declares how CI verifies the scenes under it,
   with an invisible marker line beneath the heading:
   ```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
   <!-- transcript-index: verified-by = execute -->
   ```
   The value is one or more of `execute`, `compile`, `kotlinjs`, naming
   `DemoTranscriptExecSmokeTest.EXECUTE`, `DemoTranscriptExecSmokeTest.COMPILE_ONLY` and
   `DemoTranscriptExecSmokeTest.KOTLINJS` — which is where classification is decided, and stays the
   single source of truth. An entry whose transcript is not in one of its section's declared sets is
   a failure, which is what makes the section prose ("these build and run headless", "each one
   builds and compiles in CI") an accurate statement about every entry beneath it rather than about
   most of them. The marker is an HTML comment, so it renders as nothing.
4. **Open ↗ links that exist** — a transcript is offered as an openable starting point exactly when
   the materializer ships it, i.e. when it is not in `AgentTranscriptMaterializer.EXCLUDE`. So an
   entry must carry an `assets/agent_transcripts/<name>/metadata.edn` link when its transcript is
   materialized and must not when it is not, and the committed bundle directory must really be
   there. This is the check that stops the page advertising a document the welcome screen cannot
   open.
5. **No counts in the CI paragraph** — the paragraph marked
   ```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
   <!-- transcript-index: totals -->
   ```
   must not quote a number. A paragraph that quoted the corpus size and each set's size would put
   every branch that adds a transcript into the same sentence, and any two of them into a conflict
   there. The counts live in `DemoTranscriptExecSmokeTest`, which prints them; the prose names the
   three depths without them.

### Running it

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
./gradlew checkAgentTranscriptIndex          # also runs as part of check
```
Reads five kinds of text file and nothing else: no Field server, no runloop, no boxes, no GPU.
Its heavyweight sibling `checkAgentTranscripts` builds real boxes and costs ~25 s; a completeness
check needs none of that. See `dev_docs/agent_transcript_index.md` for how to add an entry.

## AgentTranscriptLayoutGuard.kt { #agenttranscriptlayoutguard-kt }

Keeps OperationTranscript and demo boxes visible and compact, while allowing larger boards that
have a recorded reason.

A Field box frame is the labelled canvas rectangle, not its Monaco editor or output viewport. Ordinary
boxes therefore start near the positive canvas origin at roughly `300 x 100`; see
`dev_docs/agents/OPERATION_TRANSCRIPT.md`. A larger visual or capture card is allowed only when its
`file#box` key has a concrete reason in `dev_docs/agents/transcript_layout_exceptions.yaml`.

### The corpus this ceiling is stated over

Both halves: every `create` op under `dev_docs/agents/transcripts`, *and* every box in every
`metadata.edn` under `dev_docs/agents/demos`. [`AuditResult`](workspace.md#agenttranscriptlayoutguard-kt--agenttranscriptlayoutguard--auditresult) reports the two populations
separately and [`main`](workspace.md#agenttranscriptlayoutguard-kt--agenttranscriptlayoutguard--main) prints both, so "no violations" can never be read off a corpus of zero.

### A demo's transcript and its document must agree

A demo directory can hold a `build.yaml` OperationTranscript beside its `metadata.edn`, and the
transcript is what *rebuilds* the document. Those transcripts are a third population, parsed like
the corpus, and each `create` must name a box the document carries at the geometry it carries.
Agreement is what keeps a replay from writing roomy authoring frames
back over a compacted document, and it is also why those frames are not held to the ceiling a second
time: an agreeing frame *is* the document's frame, which is audited (and grandfathered) once, under
its `metadata.edn` key.

The ceiling is `620 x 170` ([`MAX_ORDINARY_WIDTH`](workspace.md#agenttranscriptlayoutguard-kt--agenttranscriptlayoutguard--max-ordinary-width), [`MAX_ORDINARY_HEIGHT`](workspace.md#agenttranscriptlayoutguard-kt--agenttranscriptlayoutguard--max-ordinary-height)). It moves together with the
ordinary box size, so a change to the house box size keeps the ratio between an ordinary box and the
ceiling the same.

Run with `./gradlew checkAgentTranscriptLayouts` (also part of `check` and `docsGates`).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/AgentTranscriptLayoutGuard.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/AgentTranscriptLayoutGuard/)

## BoxOutputChannelGuard.kt { #boxoutputchannelguard-kt }

Catches the figure that is written and then immediately erased.

`display(channel, …)` **replaces** that channel's contents rather than appending to them, so two
figures emitted to one channel from the same box leave only the second. Nothing fails, nothing
warns, and the box still looks like it worked — the last figure renders, so the loss is only
visible if you knew to expect two. Five of the eight boxes in `typography_worked_example` were in
this state, as was [`afield.audio.synth.showFaustPattern`](synthesis.md#faustpattern-kt--showfaustpattern), whose own KDoc promised "a player, a
waveform" while the waveform overwrote the player on every call.

The rule: **two figures in one box means two channels.** This guard reports any box that emits to
one channel twice.

### What counts as emitting

`display(…)` itself, plus every `fun Box.<name>(… channel: String = "…" …)` helper found in
`src/jvmMain/kotlin` — the table is read from the source rather than hardcoded, so a new `show*`
helper is covered the day it is written. A helper whose overloads disagree about the default is
skipped rather than guessed at (`logs`, `inspect`).

### Why only top-level calls

Only calls at brace depth 0 of the box's code are counted. Replacing a channel repeatedly is the
*correct* way to animate — `Box.showImg`'s KDoc calls one `display` per frame "the path an
animation wants" — so an `animate { }` body, a `for` loop or any other nested emitter is
treated as refresh, not loss.

Two emitters at depth 0 are a loss **only when that channel is not animated at all**. The
establish-animate-settle shape writes the same channel three times: once before the
loop to put the first state on screen, once per iteration inside it, and once after it so the
settled state is not up to one iteration stale. Its two depth-0 writes are the ends of one
animation, not two figures, and the first one's pixels very much do reach a screen — in
`confluence_grid` there is a `Thread.sleep(300)` immediately after it for exactly that reason.
So a channel that also receives a *nested* emission in the same box is treated as animated and
its depth-0 writes are not reported.

The cost of that narrowness is a known blind spot: `for (…) { showImg(…) }` followed by a
top-level `showMeshGrid(…)` on the same channel is a real collision this will not report, because
depth 0 sees only one emitter. The animated-channel rule widens that same blind spot rather than
guessing which loops terminate. Both are the same trade: this guard reports
a channel only when nothing in the box could have been refreshing it.

### Populations

Three: the `.yaml` box code under `dev_docs/agents/transcripts`, the `_code_.kt` box code under
`dev_docs/agents/demos`, and the library helpers themselves — a collision inside a `fun Box.…` is
worse than one in a transcript, since it ships to every caller.

Run with `./gradlew checkBoxOutputChannels` (also part of `check` and `docsGates`).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/BoxOutputChannelGuard.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/BoxOutputChannelGuard/)

## DocsSearch.kt { #docssearch-kt }

Lexical search over the documentation sources (the Markdown pages under `public/docs/`, outside
`assets/`), for Open Anything. The semantic index finds pages by meaning; this finds them by the text a reader
remembers — a page title, a heading, or an identifier from an example such as `once.renderer`,
which an embedding search ranks poorly.

Each page is split into units — its title, each heading, each fenced code block, and each prose
paragraph — and a query matches a unit when every whitespace-separated term occurs in it, case
insensitively. Hits link into the built site (`/field-docs/<page>/#<heading anchor>`), so the
index works from the Markdown alone and does not need `public/field4/` to have been built.

The index is rebuilt when any page's size or modification time changes.

## ElectronCaptureBrowser.kt { #electroncapturebrowser-kt }

This checkout's Field Electron app, driven by the server's Playwright over CDP.

The capture browser is normally a plain Chromium the server launches (`ensureSharedPlaywrightBrowser`
in `Server.kt`), which is right for everything that renders in any browser. Some output only exists
inside the Electron app — the RTT view (`afield.media.stream.ElectronRTTView`) draws frames that
Electron's `sharedTexture` delivers, and Chromium has no such API — so a capture of it has to come
from Electron itself. Playwright's Java API cannot launch Electron, but it can attach to any
Chromium over the DevTools protocol, and Electron takes `--remote-debugging-port`.

`launch` starts Electron with `APP_URL` set to the document, so its first tab is the Field page
(loaded with `field-preload.js`, the preload the RTT view needs), and [`fieldPage`](workspace.md#electroncapturebrowser-kt--electroncapturebrowser--fieldpage) finds that tab
among the window's targets (the tab strip is a separate page). Requested with
`playwright-open --electron` on the backdoor. macOS and Linux (native Wayland for the RTT view).

## KotlinSourcePartition.kt { #kotlinsourcepartition-kt }

Cuts a Kotlin source file into an ordered tree of line spans that **tiles the file exactly**.

### Why a partition, and not another parse

[`afield.runtime.completion.KotlinSourceIndex`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt-kotlinsourceindex) answers *"which declarations are in this file, and on
what line does each start?"* — which is all the completion panel, the semantic index and
[`StdlibReferenceGenerator`](workspace.md#stdlibreferencegenerator-kt-stdlibreferencegenerator) have ever needed. Rendering a source *file* as a page needs a strictly
stronger fact: **every line has to land in exactly one span**, in order, with no gaps and no
overlaps. A page that lifts KDoc into prose and puts the bodies in code fences numbered from their
real source lines is only truthful if the spans it was cut from account for the whole file. Miss
three lines and the fence below them is numbered wrong — silently, on a published page, with
nothing to notice it.

So the contract here is a *tiling*, and [`verify`](workspace.md#kotlinsourcepartition-kt--kotlinsourcepartition--verify) is the thing that proves it:

- **Tile** — the top-level spans start at line 1, each begins where the previous one ended, and the
  last ends on the file's last line.
- **Nest** — a child span lies inside its parent and after its previous sibling. Children do *not*
  tile their parent: the lines between them (a class's signature, its closing brace, the blank line
  between two members) are the parent's own text, and [`reconstruct`](workspace.md#kotlinsourcepartition-kt--kotlinsourcepartition--reconstruct) emits them from the gaps.
- **Reconstruct** — walking the tree and emitting each span's lines returns the original file, line
  for line. This is the assertion that actually has teeth; the two above are what make it debuggable
  when it fails.
- **Balance** — the code text of a `Kind.DECLARATION` span has balanced `()`, `[]` and `{}`. A span
  that stops in the middle of a body still tiles and still reconstructs, so this is the one check
  that can see a *mis-cut* rather than a lost line.

### Precision is measured, not assumed

The end of a declaration is easy when it has a brace body and awkward when it does not — an
expression body can run over as many lines as it likes, and Kotlin's continuation rules are
genuinely ambiguous without a real parser. The scanner does **not** guess: anything the
scanner cannot attribute to a declaration becomes `Kind.FILLER`, which is a span like any other and
keeps the tiling total. So a heuristic that gives up early costs *precision* (lines in FILLER) and
never *correctness* (lines lost, or attributed to the wrong declaration). [`SourcePartitionGuard`](workspace.md#sourcepartitionguard-kt-sourcepartitionguard)
fails the build on the invariants and prints the FILLER census as a number, so the imprecision is
something we can watch shrink instead of something we hope about.

### What it does not do

Bodies are not descended into: a `fun` is one span, whatever is inside it. Only container
declarations — `class`, `interface`, `object`, `enum class`, `companion object` — recurse, because
only their contents are declarations a page would want headers for. A local class inside a function
body is therefore invisible here.

Enum entries are not recognised as declarations and land in FILLER; see the census.

## MorphoDocsSupport.kt { #morphodocssupport-kt }

Lets a documentation page hold MorphoHDL itself, rather than Kotlin that mentions it.

A fence written as `data-lang=morpho` shows its body as MorphoHDL, and `public/docs_hooks.py`
wraps that body in a call into this file before the docs runner evaluates it, the same way it
already wraps a `nano` or a `forth` fence. What the reader sees under the fence is that program
compiled, grown out in full with its layout relaxing between expansions, and drawn.

The snippet is handled as a morpho box would handle it, down to using [`MorphoExecution`](languages.md#morphointerface-kt-morphoexecution)'s own
directive parsing, so a program on the page and the same text pasted into a box behave alike.
That includes the refusal: without a `# main` line there is no design to build and no width to
build it at, so the snippet fails rather than guessing. A snippet that defines no cells of its
own is given morpho's standard library, which is what makes a one-line program publishable.
`morpho_examples.md` is the page that uses this.

## SourcePageGenerator.kt { #sourcepagegenerator-kt }

Renders Kotlin source files as docs pages: KDoc as prose, declarations as headings, and the bodies
in code fences **numbered from the lines they really occupy**.

### What this is for

[`StdlibReferenceGenerator`](workspace.md#stdlibreferencegenerator-kt-stdlibreferencegenerator) answers "what is already in the box?" — a symbol per row, a summary per
symbol. It is a *summary*, and a reader who wants the next question answered ("what
does it actually do?") has to leave the site. Meanwhile the published pages cite source constantly:
`path:line` citations throughout the corpus, which are otherwise dead text. This is the destination
those two facts imply — the place a citation can point at, and the place a reference row can lead.

### Fences carry their real line numbers

A page that lifts KDoc out of the source and puts the rest in fences is only trustworthy if the
fences still say where their code lives. So every fence carries `linenums="N"` set to its real first
line, and [`verifyPage`](workspace.md#sourcepagegenerator-kt--sourcepagegenerator--verifypage) checks the published artifact rather than the intent: it parses the fences
back out of the emitted markdown and asserts that each one is **verbatim** the source lines its
`linenums` claims. Nothing else about this generator matters if that fails, which is why it runs
over every page on every invocation rather than in a test somewhere.

The cut comes from [`KotlinSourcePartition`](workspace.md#kotlinsourcepartition-kt-kotlinsourcepartition), whose tiling invariant is what makes the fences able to
account for the file in the first place; `SourcePartitionGuard` holds that end.

### Why the pages are not committed

Every other generated artifact in this repo is committed and drift-checked, and this one is not, for
a reason specific to what it contains: a source *mirror* changes whenever any line of its source
changes. Committing it would double every diff in the repository — edit a comment in `Functions.kt`
and a 10,000-line generated page changes with it — and make every source commit require a
regeneration step to keep a guard green. The reference pages are safe to commit precisely because
they summarise: they move when an API moves, not when a line does.

So these are built into the docs tree by `tools/build_zensical_docs.py` and never tracked. The cost
is that a docs build without a compiled Kotlin tree has no source pages, which is handled where it
shows: `rewrite_source_citations` in `public/docs_hooks.py` links a citation only when its page was
generated, so the pages degrade to plain chips rather than to dead links.

### Running it

```diffstatic {data-lang=bash}
./gradlew generateSourcePages                     # into build/source-pages
./gradlew checkSourcePages                        # verify only, no output kept
```

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/SourcePageGenerator.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/SourcePageGenerator/)

## SourcePartitionGuard.kt { #sourcepartitionguard-kt }

Proves that every Kotlin file in the repository can be cut into spans **losslessly**, and measures
how much of it the cutter actually understands.

### The failure this exists to stop

A source page that lifts KDoc into prose, turns declarations into headers and numbers the code
fences from their real source lines is correct only if the partition it was rendered from accounts
for the whole file. Lose three lines and every fence below them is numbered wrong — on a published
page, in a way that looks completely normal, and that a reader can only catch by opening the source
they came here to avoid opening. The wrong page is well-formed, so review does not catch it either.

So the partition is checked against the file it came from, over the whole repository, before any
page exists. [`KotlinSourcePartition.verify`](workspace.md#kotlinsourcepartition-kt--kotlinsourcepartition--verify) holds the invariants; this walks the corpus, adds the
two checks that need more than one file's worth of context, and reports.

### What it checks

- **The invariants** — tile, nest, reconstruct, balance, terminated. See [`KotlinSourcePartition`](workspace.md#kotlinsourcepartition-kt-kotlinsourcepartition).
- **Agreement** — every declaration `KotlinSourceIndex.parseTopLevelDefinitions` finds is the
  `declarationLine` of some `DECLARATION` span. Two independent recognisers, one corpus: a
  disagreement means one of them is wrong about real source, and it does not much matter which,
  because the reference pages and the completion panel are built on the index while the source pages
  would be built on this. They have to see the same declarations or the two halves of the site
  disagree.
- **The unattributed census, as a ratchet** — every line the partition could not attribute to a
  declaration, a comment or a header lands in `FILLER`. That is a *correctness-preserving* fallback:
  the tiling still holds, no line is lost. It is not free, though — a `FILLER` line is a line a page
  can only show as anonymous code — so the `FILLER` lines that carry code are counted and pinned,
  and the pin falls whenever the scanner learns a shape and rises only with a reason. Blank lines
  land in `FILLER` too and are not counted: there is nothing for a page to lose.
- **Locals reported as API** — a second ratchet counts the declarations
  [`KotlinSourceIndex`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt-kotlinsourceindex) reports from *inside a function body*, each of which the reference pages and
  the completion panel would otherwise publish as though it were public.

### Running it

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
./gradlew checkSourcePartition                        # also part of check and docsGates
./gradlew checkSourcePartition --args=--verbose       # …and the per-file and per-shape breakdowns
```
Needs no Field server, no GPU and no network: it reads source text. Sibling of
[`KDocAttachmentGuard`](workspace.md#kdocattachmentguard-kt-kdocattachmentguard), which guards the other half of the same pipeline — that a KDoc block reaches
the declaration its author meant.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/SourcePartitionGuard.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/SourcePartitionGuard/)

## StdlibReferenceGenerator.kt { #stdlibreferencegenerator-kt }

Emits Field's **codebase reference** — the browsable answer to "what is already in the box?" —
from the KDoc that lives next to the code.

### Why this exists, and why it is not Dokka

Dokka was removed in `20e64da5`, because the durable facts belong in KDoc beside the code and a
generated wall of one-page-per-symbol HTML is not documentation anyone reads. Field already has
two *interactive* ways into that KDoc — the completion panel's recursive code browser
(`public/docs/completion_doc_browser.md`) and the semantic index — but both need you to already
know the name you are looking for. Nothing answered the browsing question. This generator does,
with ordinary Zensical markdown inside the existing docs site: a page per completion category,
a section per source file, the file's own KDoc as the orientation prose, and a table per type.

### One parser, not two

Declarations come from `KotlinSourceIndex.parseTopLevelDefinitions` — the *same* scan that feeds
the in-app completion doc browser — so a symbol listed here is by construction a symbol the doc
panel can resolve. Only the signature text is re-read from source here (the index stores names
and lines, not signatures); see `signatureAt`.

### What it will not invent

- Every summary is the first paragraph of a real KDoc comment; a symbol with no KDoc is listed
  with an empty summary rather than a guessed one.
- A KDoc reference in square brackets is linkified only when the target is a type this reference
  actually emits — the same "links only appear when they resolve" rule the completion panel
  follows. Everything else degrades to plain inline code.
- The "see also" links from a reference section to a worked-example page are *evidence-based*:
  a page is linked only when it literally mentions `MIN_EVIDENCE_HITS` or more distinct public
  symbol names from that source file (see `evidenceLinks`). No hand-maintained topic map to rot.

### File overview rule

The first KDoc block in a file is treated as the *file's* overview when it ends before the first
declaration **and** is separated from that declaration by at least one blank or comment line —
and it is then not also shown as that declaration's own summary. A block written flush against
its declaration stays that declaration's own KDoc, of which only the first paragraph is
published; the file's "what it is" cell on the index then has nothing to fill it with.

### Running it

Regenerate the committed pages (needs no Field server, no GPU, no network):
```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
./gradlew generateCodebaseReference
```
Run with **no** output directory and it emits to a temp dir and then **drift-checks** the
committed pages byte-for-byte instead — which is what the `docs.codebase-reference.generate`
FIELD_TEST does, so an API or KDoc change that nobody regenerated fails the build. This mirrors
[`afield.examples.AgentTranscriptMaterializer`](examples.md#agenttranscriptmaterializer-kt-agenttranscriptmaterializer) and the `tools/linalg-generator --check` mode that
guards `public/docs/linear_algebra_api.md`.

The pages are **committed** rather than built on the fly: the Zensical docs build must not gain a
JVM step, and a generated reference is only trustworthy if an API change shows up as a reviewable
diff.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/StdlibReferenceGenerator.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/StdlibReferenceGenerator/)

## canvasFlightRecording.kt { #canvasflightrecording-kt }

Filming a canvas flight to MP4, one frame at a time.

[`recordCanvasFlight`](workspace.md#canvasflightrecording-kt--recordcanvasflight) drives the flight's clock in the capture page (the server's Playwright page, or
the Electron window after `playwright-open --electron`): for each frame it sets the time
(`window.fieldCanvasFlight.seek`, `CanvasFlightClient` in the frontend), waits until the browser has
painted that frame, captures it over CDP and pipes the JPEG to ffmpeg. Nothing runs on the wall
clock, so a frame that takes a second to capture is the same frame as one that takes ten
milliseconds, and a loaded machine films the same movie as an idle one. Live screen capture would
drop frames instead.

The page is sized for the film first (`width` by `height` pixels at `pixelRatio`, through CDP device
metrics) and put back afterwards. The report says how many frames were captured and encoded (counted
again by ffprobe), and for every stop the frame that reaches it and the camera in that frame.

## doc.kt { #doc-kt }

Exports a Field document to documentation pages, and the capture helpers that export uses.

[`exportToDocumentation`](workspace.md#doc-kt--exporttodocumentation) walks the boxes under a root that carry documentation metadata and writes
Markdown pages with their captured assets into a docs directory. [`splitKotlinIntoChunks`](workspace.md#doc-kt--splitkotlinintochunks) and
[`CommentCommandRewriter`](workspace.md#doc-kt-commentcommandrewriter) cut box code into the pieces a page shows, and [`format`](workspace.md#doc-kt--format) expands a box's
text into page Markdown.

The rest of the file is capture plumbing: [`processPng`](workspace.md#doc-kt--processpng) for still images,
[`Window.raiseAndScreenshot`](workspace.md#doc-kt--raiseandscreenshot), [`Window.raiseAndRecord`](workspace.md#doc-kt--raiseandrecord) and [`captureGlfwWindow`](workspace.md#doc-kt--captureglfwwindow) for native renderer
windows, and an ffmpeg layer ([`FFMPEG`](workspace.md#doc-kt--ffmpeg), [`runProcessLogged`](workspace.md#doc-kt--runprocesslogged), [`detectCropBox`](workspace.md#doc-kt--detectcropbox),
[`encodeWithCropAndMargin`](workspace.md#doc-kt--encodewithcropandmargin)) for recordings.

## KDocExtractor.kt { #kdocextractor-kt }

Reads the KDoc comments out of a Kotlin source file and attaches each one to the declaration below it.

[`KDocExtractor.extractKDocs`](workspace.md#kdocextractor-kt--kdocextractor--extractkdocs) returns one [`KDocComment`](workspace.md#kdocextractor-kt-kdoccomment) per block, with its line span and the name and
kind of the declaration it documents. The completion doc panel, `KotlinSourceIndex` and the generated
reference pages all read summaries through it. A block attaches to the first following line that
`parseDeclaration` recognises; `KDocAttachmentGuard` reports blocks that would attach to the wrong
declaration.

## pageFilm.kt { #pagefilm-kt }

Filming any web page frame by frame: the page filmer behind `film-page` on the backdoor.

The canvas flight ([`recordCanvasFlight`](workspace.md#canvasflightrecording-kt--recordcanvasflight)) drives Field's own canvas. Some things worth filming are
other pages: a chat lens exported to a standalone HTML file, a three.js view on its own page. [`filmPage`](workspace.md#pagefilm-kt--filmpage)
opens the page in a capture context of its own (so the shared Field page is untouched), runs a setup
script, then steps a frame script through the film's clock, waiting for each frame to paint before it
captures it and pipes it to ffmpeg, exactly as the flight does. Each script's answer is JSON text
("null" for none): `evaluateWithin` waits for a truthy answer, and an `undefined` would run it again.

## screenshot.kt { #screenshot-kt }

Screenshot and video capture of Field's browser UI, used by the backdoor and the docs runner.

Captures go through the server's shared Playwright page. [`captureBoxScreenshot`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--captureboxscreenshot) and
[`captureWindowScreenshot`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--capturewindowscreenshot) answer the agent capture requests for one box's output or the whole
window, [`openEditorForCapture`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--openeditorforcapture) opens a box's editor first so inline visualizers are on screen, and
[`captureBoxVideo`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--captureboxvideo) and [`captureWindowVideo`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--capturewindowvideo) record frames over CDP and encode them to MP4 with
ffmpeg. Before each capture a preparation script waits for the page to settle, with every wait
bounded so that a page that never paints fails with a message naming what was pending.
[`trimUniformEdgePixels`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--trimuniformedgepixels) crops uniform borders from the result.

[`DocsUiDriver`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt-docsuidriver) is the object a docs `drive` script uses to act on the page during a recording,
and [`DocsUiRecorder`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt-docsuirecorder) runs the recording beside it. [`Box.screenshot`](workspace.md#screenshot-kt--screenshot) is the box-code entry point.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/tools/docs/screenshot.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/screenshot/)

### DocsUiDriver { #screenshot-kt-docsuidriver }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DocsUiDriver</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pageProvider</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Page</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/tools/docs/screenshot/#L2880)

Every method marshals onto the Playwright dispatcher and blocks the calling (main runloop) thread for the result, so scripts never touch the thread-bound `Page` directly. `wait` sleeps on the *calling* thread, leaving the Playwright thread free to keep grabbing recorder frames.

## EffectiveParameter.kt { #effectiveparameter-kt }

A bounded scalar parameter that keeps the value it was asked for apart from the value it uses.

[`EffectiveParameter`](workspace.md#effectiveparameter-kt-effectiveparameter) stores the requested value as written and reports [`EffectiveParameter.effective`](workspace.md#effectiveparameter-kt--effectiveparameter--effective)
as that value coerced into `minimum..maximum`, with [`EffectiveParameter.clamped`](workspace.md#effectiveparameter-kt--effectiveparameter--clamped) saying whether the
two differ. [`EffectiveParameter.snapshot`](workspace.md#effectiveparameter-kt--effectiveparameter--snapshot) reads both at once into a [`ParameterValue`](workspace.md#effectiveparameter-kt-parametervalue). Nothing in
`src/jvmMain` constructs one yet; `EffectiveParameterTest` covers the behaviour.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ui/controls/EffectiveParameter.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/controls/EffectiveParameter/)

## LineNotes.kt { #linenotes-kt }

Line notes: the sentence, and sometimes a picture, that the editor shows for one line of a box's program.

Languages register a [`LineNotes.Provider`](workspace.md#linenotes-kt--linenotes--provider) for the property their programs live in; the editor asks through a `line-note` request.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ui/output/LineNotes.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/)

### LineNotes { #linenotes-kt-linenotes }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">LineNotes</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L64)

What a box's program shows at one of its lines — a sentence, and a picture when there is one — offered wherever the editor looks at a line: at the top of the completion popup opened on it, and in the notes beside the cursor.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="linenotes-kt--linenotes--note"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Note</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">caption</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">png</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ByteArray</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">volatile</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">meta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Segment</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyList</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">imageScale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L70) | A line's note: `caption` a sentence about it, `png` a small picture of what it evaluates to, or null. `volatile` says the note can change while the text does not — a last run's value, which the next run replaces, or its age — so the editor asks again rather than keeping it against the text. |
| <a id="linenotes-kt--linenotes--segment"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Segment</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">strong</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L88) | A run of a note's `Note.value`: `strong` for a result — a number, a stack value, an answer count. |
| <a id="linenotes-kt--linenotes--plain"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">plain</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L93) | A plain run of a note's value. |
| <a id="linenotes-kt--linenotes--strong"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">strong</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L96) | A result in a note's value, which the editor sets in bold. |
| <a id="linenotes-kt--linenotes--provider"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">Provider</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L99) | Describes [`line`](visualization.md#notation-kt--line) (1-based) of `source`, the text of [`box`](workspace.md#boxes-kt--box)'s property as the editor holds it; null when it has nothing to say. |
| <a id="linenotes-kt--linenotes--register"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">register</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">applies</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="kc">true</span> <span class="p">}</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">provider</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Provider</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/LineNotes/#L113) | Offer notes for `property` of the boxes `applies` accepts. Registrations that accept a box are asked newest first, and the first note wins; a provider with nothing to say returns null and the next is asked. Providers are called off the main thread, one at a time, and may take a moment — a picture is usually rendered — so they should cache. |

## stdlib_output.kt { #stdlib-output-kt }

HTML-safe syntax colouring for a value printed into a box output.

[`highlightSyntax`](workspace.md#stdlib-output-kt--highlightsyntax) escapes a string and wraps its numbers, punctuation and brackets in spans, so
the result reads as code rather than as prose. It is purely lexical and language-agnostic: it
finds floats, integers, single punctuation characters and brackets, and knows nothing of
keywords, strings or comments. Everything else is escaped, so the result is always safe to drop
into HTML. `String.h` and `String.ss` are the same call, shorter.

One of the `stdlib` files, which the `intro` preamble star-imports into every box, so everything
here can be called unqualified, with `Box` as the implicit receiver.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ui/output/stdlib_output.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ui/output/stdlib_output/)
